summary: Abstract Let ρ₅ᴿ be the largest element growth possible in exact Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting on real 5 × 5 matrices, with every legal choice at a pivot tie allowed. We prove ρ₅ᴿ = α = 4.132517078632472854223346853277…, where α is the algebraic lower bound identified by Chen, Edelman, and Urschel, specified by their degree-61 polynomial and a rational isolating interval. Our contribution is the global upper bound. An exact inverse-elimination representation retains all initial and intermediate entry bounds of the same matrix. A constructive contraction preserves the final-pivot height while reducing the problem to two saturated tail geometries. On the negative-diagonal geometry, three feasible paths eliminate six variables and give an attained fibre maximum over seventeen shared parameters. Rational certificates control the remaining domains, while a constrained algebraic maximum argument and feasible transports resolve regions meeting the sharp value. The proof combines these analytic reductions with exact verification of a finite, complete cover. We provide a partial Lean formalization together with publicly available exact certificates and verification code. Files and supporting materials This record contains the 56-page manuscript and its 7-page supplementary index. Both PDFs are archived unchanged from the fixed GitHub release v1.0.1. The supplementary index maps proof responsibilities S1–S8 to the original proof objects and verifier entry points. Source code, exact certificates, verification guides and file manifests are available at GitHub release v1.0.1 . The original certificate assets remain frozen under v1.0.0 and are linked from that release. Formalization scope The recorded first-phase Lean project cold rebuild passed 634 product modules, three additional example/audit modules and 47 named axiom checks, using an explicit dependency-order driver with pinned third-party caches reused and supplemented. The final sharp Lean equality remains conditional on XGlobalSafety and RootEndpointSafety. This is a partial Lean formalization accompanying the computer-assisted proof; neither a complete unconditional Lean proof nor formal verification of the Python/C++ acceptor implementations is claimed. The frozen PDFs retain the publication-status wording at the time of their GitHub release; this Zenodo record supplies their archival deposit.
title: The exact maximum growth factor for complete pivoting on real 5 × 5 matrices

summary: The translation of emotional language in literary discourse involves not only the transfer of lexical meaning but also the reconstruction of emotional intensity, evaluative connotation, psychological stance, and pragmatic effect. The present study investigates lexical-emotional transformations in the Arabic translation of Abdulla Qodiriy’s novel O‘tkan kunlar, published in Arabic as Al-Ayyām al-Khawālī ( الأيام الخوالي ) in 2024. The research is based on a comparative linguopragmatic analysis of emotionally marked units selected from the Uzbek source text and their Arabic correspondences. The examples were examined according to three interrelated parameters: semantic content, emotional intensity, and pragmatic function. The analysis revealed several recurrent patterns, including direct emotional correspondence, grammatical recategorization, semantic-pragmatic attenuation, preservation of emotional intensity, contextual specification, and metaphorical-emotional recreation. The findings demonstrate that lexical-semantic equivalence does not necessarily guarantee an equivalent emotional effect. In some cases, Arabic preserves both the type and intensity of the source emotion; in others, the emotional meaning is attenuated or conceptually reorganized. Conversely, metaphorical emotion may be successfully recreated through a different but functionally corresponding lexical image. The study therefore argues that emotional translation should be assessed beyond lexical equivalence by considering the degree to which the target text reconstructs the emotional and pragmatic potential of the source expression.
tags: literary translation, emotional language, linguopragmatics, Abdulla Qodiriy, O'tkan kunlar, Arabic translation, emotional intensity, pragmatic equivalence, lexical transformation.
title: EMOTIONAL TRANSFORMATIONS IN THE ARABIC TRANSLATION OF ABDULLA QODIRIY'S O'TKAN KUNLAR (BYGONE DAYS): A LINGUOPRAGMATIC ANALYSIS

summary: Patinae v0.5.0 Zawinski's law says that programs keep expanding until they can read email. Patinae started as a molecular viewer. It now has background tasks, Markdown output, and an AI plugin that can connect to MCP servers. We appear to be one mail server away from compliance. The largest change in 0.5.0 is underneath all of that: the task system has been completely rebuilt around one shared lifecycle . Loading a structure, running a script, and asking a plugin to do background work now use the same rules for completion, progress, errors, and cancellation. Those rules extend across the desktop application, native plugins, IPC, Python, and the web viewer. That gives plugins the foundation for longer workflows. A plugin can issue a command, receive its actual result, wait for any background work it starts, and decide what to do next. The new AI plugin puts that into practice: ask for a scene in ordinary language, let the agent operate Patinae, and have it inspect the rendered image before answering. Highlights A task has one lifecycle, wherever it starts Background work now receives a host-assigned task ID and stays under the shared task runner's control. Progress, diagnostics, final outcomes, and cancellation requests belong to that task. The desktop shows active tasks with progress and cancellation controls, and services background work independently of rendering. The distinction between accepting a command and finishing its work is explicit. An immediate command returns its result. A command that starts background work also returns task IDs, which clients can observe, wait for, or cancel. Success means the required scene changes have been applied; it does not promise that the GPU has already presented a frame. Scripts and plugin workflows can create child tasks. A parent stays active until its children finish, and cancellation propagates through the task tree. Cancelling stops further work cooperatively; changes already applied to the scene remain. A wait timeout ends the wait without cancelling the underlying task. Python command methods wait for background work by default, so a script can fetch a structure and then operate on it. Use wait=False to get task IDs immediately and manage them through tasks or a notebook viewer's view.tasks . Browser integrations receive command results and use viewer.tasks.get , list , wait , and cancel to follow the same lifecycle. Plugins can coordinate work and recover from errors Plugins now receive typed replies to the host commands they issue, correlated to the original request and delivered only to the requesting plugin. Replies include success or failure, output messages, and every accepted task ID. A command can fail after starting some work, so those IDs remain available for inspection. For plugin authors, the new contract separates responsibilities clearly: The host owns task identity and state. A plugin submits a task request and starts its worker after the host accepts it and delivers the assigned ID. Workers report progress, output, and completion. Scene mutations go through the host and must be acknowledged before the plugin reports success. Nested commands belong to the parent task. Their completion and cancellation participate in the same lifecycle. Recovery can be deliberate. Child failure fails the parent by default. An executor can opt into deciding the parent outcome after inspecting and handling a failed child. The original failure remains in task history. This matters for an agent that needs to correct a command, or a script that has a fallback when a download fails. The parent can handle the error and continue while preserving the record of what happened. Silent execution also follows the task tree. It suppresses REPL presentation while retaining results, diagnostics, and logs, so a plugin can handle intermediate failures without filling the output panel with messages it intends to recover from. Polling plugins additionally receive named selections and Recent Atoms path

summary: The research paper titled "The Ocean and Spatial Representation in Sangam Literature" by Dr. K. Periya Karuppan examines how the marine ecosystem of the Neithal landscape (ocean and coastal regions) is constructed as a literary and cultural space ( Idanaakkam ) in classical Tamil poetry. Drawing contextual evidence from texts such as Purananuru, Akananuru, Aingurunuru, Natrinai, Paripadal , and the epic Silappathikaram , the study explores the multifaceted thematic functions of the sea. It analyzes the ocean as a metaphorical space for the rising sun, symbolizing a king’s fierce wrath, and as a physical benchmark to measure the profound depth of the hero’s love. The author highlights the realistic environmental depictions of the coast, including the pervasive fishy odor ( Pulal Naatram ) of the waves and drying fish, contrasted with the fragrant Thazhai and Punnai blossoms. Furthermore, the paper looks into the stark demographic contrast between the small, humble coastal hamlets ( Sirugudi ) of the Parathavar community and the immense, vast ocean where their large ships ( Vangam/Thimil ) vanish into the horizon. Lastly, the study maps the sea as a locus for natural phenomenon, like the water cycle, and as a stage for mythological history, notably Murugan's triumph over Surapadman. The paper concludes that Sangam poets seamlessly blended geographic realities with human emotions to transform the physical ocean into a vital psychological space.

summary: Resumo O Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) constitui uma das principais conquistas institucionais do Brasil, ao estabelecer a saúde como direito universal em um país continental e profundamente desigual. Quase quatro décadas após sua criação, o desafio central não é reconstruí-lo, mas transformar sua ampla estrutura em um sistema efetivamente integrado, resolutivo, sustentável e preparado para as mudanças demográficas, epidemiológicas e tecnológicas do século XXI. Essa transformação exige ampliar e qualificar o financiamento público. Em 2024, o gasto governamental em saúde correspondeu a 5,03% do PIB. Entretanto, em 2019, o setor público respondeu por apenas cerca de 40% do gasto total em saúde, enquanto aproximadamente 60% foram financiados por fontes privadas, proporção inversa à observada na maioria dos sistemas universais e muito inferior à média pública de aproximadamente 72% nos países da OCDE. O subfinanciamento transfere custos às famílias, especialmente por meio da compra de medicamentos, mas aumentar recursos sem melhorar a organização não será suficiente. O artigo propõe avançar da descentralização para uma regionalização efetiva, com listas de espera transparentes, compras em escala e integração entre atenção primária, especialistas, hospitais e cuidados domiciliares. A extensa rede territorial do SUS deve assumir maior responsabilidade pela saúde de populações definidas, com capacidade diagnóstica, acompanhamento longitudinal e atuação preventiva. Dados interoperáveis devem ser tratados como infraestrutura pública estratégica. Inteligência artificial, genômica, telessaúde, monitoramento remoto e medicina de precisão somente produzirão valor se forem validados na população brasileira, incorporados a fluxos assistenciais funcionais e avaliados quanto a benefício clínico, custo-efetividade, segurança e equidade. Diante do envelhecimento populacional, o SUS precisa evoluir para um sistema de saúde que aprende continuamente, antecipa riscos, mede resultados, amplia o que funciona e abandona intervenções de baixo valor.   Summary The Brazilian Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS) is one of Brazil’s most important institutional achievements, establishing health as a universal right in a continental and deeply unequal country. Nearly four decades after its creation, the central challenge is not to rebuild the SUS, but to transform its extensive infrastructure into a genuinely integrated, effective, sustainable system prepared for the demographic, epidemiological, and technological changes of the twenty-first century. This transformation requires both increasing and improving public financing. In 2024, government health expenditure corresponded to 5.03% of GDP. However, in 2019, the public sector accounted for only approximately 40% of total health spending, while around 60% came from private sources—the reverse of the pattern observed in most universal health systems and well below the OECD average public share of approximately 72%. Underfunding shifts healthcare costs to households, particularly through medicine purchases, but increasing resources without improving organization will not be sufficient. The article proposes moving from decentralization toward effective regionalization, supported by transparent waiting lists, procurement at scale, and integration among primary care, specialists, hospitals, and home care. summary: We propose the Encephlian Standard Format (ESF), a 19-channel international 10–20 montage at 250 Hz, average re-referenced, microvolt-calibrated, and channel-wise robust z-scored, as a deterministic canonical representation for deploying pretrained EEG classifiers on heterogeneous acquisition hardware, paired with a recoverability framework that predicts which signal-level shifts ESF can and cannot recover. On the Temple University Abnormal EEG Corpus (TUAB, n = 276 patient-stratified, 253 unique patients), a frozen EEGPT linear probe attains clean AUROC 0.908. We sweep five acquisition-shift axes (native sampling rate, per-channel gain, 50 Hz line noise, electrode montage, and broadband signal-to-noise) and show that left-invertible and bandwidth-preserving operators are (f,0)-recoverable while sub-Nyquist sampling and broadband Gaussian noise are not (Propositions 1, 2). A Pinsker-based AUROC–total-variation bound holds on 18/18 measured axis-arms (median implied constant 0.10). Clustering every recording by its joint behaviour across the sweep yields seven failure categories: 100% of baseline-correct normals flip on at least one shifted cell, 95.3% flip with confidence ≥ 0.80 into the abnormal class, while 87.4% of baseline-correct abnormals are robust-correct. Shift preferentially converts clean normals into confident abnormal reports, the worst direction for screening. Code, perturbation operators, the ESF reference implementation, and per-recording predictions are released. Preprint of the manuscript submitted to the IEEE Signal Processing in Medicine and Biology Symposium (SPMB) 2026 on 30 June 2026, currently under review. Code, perturbation operators, and per-recording predictions are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22727770 and maintained at https://github.com/h5371h/esf-recoverability. The supplementary material is included as a second file.
title: ESF: A Canonical Representation and Recoverability Framework for Deploying Pretrained EEG Classifiers in Heterogeneous Clinics

summary: QN-AEI is a curated, simulation-based benchmark for studying quantum noise effects in amplitude-encoded grayscale images. Two hundred images from the BSDS500 training subset were converted to grayscale, resized to 64 x 64 pixels, and encoded as 4096-dimensional normalized amplitude vectors, each corresponding to a 12-qubit quantum state. Every image was then evolved under three completely positive trace-preserving noise channels — amplitude damping, Pauli-Z dephasing, and depolarizing noise — at four channel-parameter values, eta = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, with 200 repeated stochastic realizations per image-channel-noise configuration. The release therefore contains 2,400 image-channel-noise conditions, 480,000 noisy amplitude-encoded realizations, and 1,966,080,000 normalized perturbation samples. Each image-level record stores the preprocessed clean image, the clean amplitude vector, the noisy statevector matrices, raw and pooled perturbation arrays, normalized bounded-domain perturbation values, and structured condition-level metadata including a deterministic per-condition random seed. The release also includes a dataset manifest, source-image provenance linking every record to its BSDS500 original, an automated validation report covering all 200 records, aggregated and condition-level perturbation statistics, and the MATLAB script used to generate and validate the dataset. The original BSDS500 image files are not redistributed. Users should obtain them from the Berkeley Computer Vision Group and comply with the BSDS500 usage terms. The dataset supports reproducible benchmarking of quantum-noise modeling, bounded-domain perturbation modeling, denoising and error-mitigation methods, and uncertainty and reliability analysis using the repeated realizations. Due to the size of the release (12.6 GB) and Zenodo's current infrastructure load, QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip is distributed as 26 sequential parts (QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part001 through QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part026) rather than a single file. summary: We present a synthesis of the Karimov–Alekberli (KA) Framework into a unified theory of Constitutional Intelligence: the capacity of an adaptive system to make consequential decisions that are simultaneously governed, explainable, accountable, reconstructable, verifiable, and capable of learning without retroactive falsification of the historical record. We formulate six formal results — one per required property — organized into three proof tiers: Tier A (two unconditional geometric results), Tier B (three conditional results valid under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), Tier C (one KA extension under a physical implementation assumption). Results draw on viability theory,information geometry, and thermodynamics. The theorems are organized in three tiers reflecting their current proof status: Tier A (fully proved geometric results), Tier B (conditional theorems under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), and Tier C (KA extensions requiring additional physical or topological conditions). A unifying condition, the Constitutional Integrity Criterion (CIC), is formulated as a representation theorem characterizing systems that satisfy all six properties simultaneously. We derive, under the CIC, that the governance loop Govern → Reason → Act → Remember → Learn → Govern defines a well-defined autonomous map on the constitutional moduli space that preserves the admissible region; fixed-point existence follows as a corollary under compactness. We position the framework within the existing literature on viability theory, formal verification, safe reinforcement learning, AI governance, and constitutional economics. We propose Constitutional Intelligence Science as the emerging discipline that unifies these results.
title: Constitutional Intelligence as Formal Science The Karimov–Alekberli Framework as Mathematical Foundation for Governed Institutional Cognition

summary: Adaptability release: the analysis pipeline no longer assumes an NV-scale emitter or a negligible instrument response, and measured data enter through a documented file contract. This release also upgrades the fit physics itself -- two changes that came out of adversarial re-examination rather than feature work. Bring your own emitter and instrument load_hbt_csv / save_hbt_csv : a documented two-column contract ( delay_ns,counts ) with an exact round trip and refusals for wrong headers, field counts, negative counts and non-increasing delay axes. Configurable lifetime windows : t1_bounds / t2_bounds (ns) on analyze_histogram , fit_g2_histogram and profile_likelihood_ci -- validated on entry. The defaults are the NV-scale window used since v0.1. The test suite runs a tau1 = 0.15 ns, tau2 = 5 ns emitter and shows BOTH halves: the default window fails visibly (error > 0.2), the emitter's own window recovers g2(0) to better than 0.05. register_platform (existing) plus a test that a user-defined platform runs the whole pipeline; load_fisequr now takes the dataset directory explicitly instead of defaulting to one machine's path. The fit physics, corrected Physical parameterization. The LM fit and the profile likelihood now fit the dip depth rho^2 multiplying BOTH exponentials (g2(0) = 1 - rho^2), the form g2_measured itself uses. The previous 1 - d e1 + a e2 form capped d at 1 -- which biased g2(0) upward for any emitter with a strong bunching shoulder -- and hid a genuine (d, a) ridge behind that cap. The instrument response is in the model. Both fitters now use the closed-form Gaussian-convolved exponentials at cfg.sigma_irf , so the estimand is the IRF-free g2(0), not the softened dip the raw histogram shows; a test constructs a case where the two differ by more than 0.02 and checks the right one is recovered. An honest interval, and the knob that tightens it. With the normalization free, a slow bunching shoulder trades almost exactly against the flat level -- a real near-degeneracy of the histogram alone (probed directly during development: the exact-Poisson likelihood is flat to Delta NLL ~ 1 from g2 = 0.10 to 0.30 in the demonstration case). The profile interval now says so by being wide. The information that breaks the tie is the independently measured singles rate: pass r_hat from the counters and c0_prior=(1.0, sd) at their precision, and the interval tightens to what the data genuinely support (covering the truth and shrinking ~2.7x from 10 s to 60 s in the tests). Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated) CSV contract: exact round trip; four distinct malformed-file refusals. Fast-emitter recovery only with its own window, and visible failure without it. IRF-aware estimand: the profile CI covers the IRF-free g2(0) where the IRF-softened value is more than 0.02 higher. Profile CI with the singles-rate prior: covers the truth at 10 s and 60 s, width shrinks by more than 2x; with the normalization free it stays covering but wider -- the degeneracy is reported, not hidden. Window validation: malformed bounds raise in both fitters. 67 tests across Python 3.9-3.13 (ML tests skip without torch). Install: pip install -U sparq-triage .
title: SPARQ: spiking physics-in-the-loop autonomous reinforcement triage of quantum emitters

summary: Doucette rereads Keynes’s 1930 essay “Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren” as a sequencing rule, not a prophecy of mass idleness or automatic leisure. Keynes defined technological unemployment as a pace problem: labor-saving discovery outruns new uses for labor. He called it a temporary maladjustment, while predicting long-run abundance through technical progress and capital accumulation. Doucette applies this framework to the U.S. mid-2020s, focusing on generative AI’s early labor-market effects and the data-center buildout. AI stress appears mainly in junior cognitive work and entry-level hiring, not the national unemployment rate. Data centers are capital-intensive, labor-sparse operations: thousands of construction jobs, few permanent ones, and local conflict over water, power, rates, and consent. They resemble power stations or switching offices more than factories. Northern Virginia illustrates the consent problem. Keynes said little about ownership, so the paper imports distribution: who captures the dividend? It proposes three tests: absorption (rebuild the first rung), cost assignment (large loads pay incremental infrastructure costs), and the dividend (where productivity appears). It considers accelerationist, localist, and leisure-skeptic objections. Limitations include early evidence, mixed data, and one mature cluster. The conclusion separates two clocks: short-run maladjustment and long-run abundance. AI is neither a completed solution nor a surplus of workers; it changes task content and drives physical accumulation. The task is to keep entry paths open, assign costs to the load causing them, and track whether productivity reaches typical pay. Failure would be institutional, not technical.
title: The New Disease and the Machine Room: Keynes's 1930 Essay, Artificial Intelligence, and the Data-Center Buildout

summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.
title: Runtime-State Watermarking in Transformers: A Controlled Protocol for Distinguishing Static Self-Simulation from Runtime-State Decodability

summary: Experimental-adaptability release: the three inputs a laboratory actually has -- a measured dispersion table, a fixed set of deposited materials, and a reflectance specification -- now enter the yield-aware design loop directly. Added TabulatedMaterial : bring your measured dispersion. An n(lam) table from ellipsometry, a vendor datasheet or a refractiveindex.info tabulation is used directly -- no Sellmeier fit required. Shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation, refusal outside the tabulated range (the same rule as the cited Sellmeier built-ins), and a mandatory reference naming where the table comes from. An optional extinction column serves the absorbing forward solver through .nk() ; .n() refuses an absorbing table rather than silently dropping k, because the design path is lossless. .n(lam) is the same interface as SellmeierMaterial.n , so a tabulated material drops into dispersion_shape , layer_index and everything built on them. Per-layer and frozen design boxes. Every DesignBox bound now accepts a scalar or an (N,) array, and a bound pair with lo == hi freezes that parameter -- so a real multi-material stack, whose indices are deposited materials rather than design variables, runs through the identical engine. DesignBox.thickness_only(N, t_lo, t_hi, n_fixed) builds the common case. A fully frozen box (nothing left to design) is refused. weights_from_reflectance : mirror and high-reflector merits. A reflectance-based linear merit converts to transmittance weights by the exact lossless identity R = 1 - T, so reflectance specifications run through the same hand adjoint, design engine and CVaR robustifier unchanged. The thickness-only metrology path , documented and anchored: a tool that logs thickness but not per-run index sets n_fab = n_recipe in the trace contract; the fitted twin then invents no index errors, and robustification on a frozen-index box uses exactly the information the lab has. Changed FabTwinConfig validates its bounds (strictly increasing scalars): the learned twin's recipe conditioner normalizes by hi - lo, so frozen or per-layer bounds -- a design-space feature of DesignBox -- are refused there with an explanation instead of producing a division by zero. Anchors (asserted in tests/test_experimental_adapt.py , not stated) A table sampled from the cited Malitson Sellmeier is exact at its nodes and agrees with the independent closed form between them; the whole design path (shape, solver, hand adjoint vs central finite differences) runs on a tabulated material end to end. The design engine and the CVaR robustifier return a frozen index profile EXACTLY ( np.array_equal ); per-layer sampling and clipping respect each layer's window. The reflectance-weight identity holds at machine precision on a lossless stack through the solver's exact R + T = 1; on an absorbing stack it fails by exactly w_R . A (asserted as an exact relation), and the quarter-wave (HL)^3 mirror scores its closed-form admittance reflectance through this path. A thickness-only twin's sampled index errors stay below 1e-3 while its thickness errors are preserved, and CVaR ascent on the frozen-index box does not degrade the objective it ascends. summary: Adaptability release: sqzcomb now speaks laboratory units and fits measured data, so the normalized-units engine underneath is usable directly from an experiment. Added sqzcomb.physical : the exact dictionary between laboratory ring parameters and the package's normalized LLE frame. RingSpec (loaded linewidth in Hz, escape efficiency, single-photon Kerr shift, pump wavelength -- with a mandatory reference naming where the numbers come from) plus normalized_pump , threshold_power , normalized_detuning , normalized_dispersion , normalized_frequency / physical_frequency , and intracavity_photons . Conventions are checked by identities rather than trusted: every conversion round-trips exactly, F scales as sqrt(P), and threshold_power is cross-validated through the package's own flat-state cubic -- at the returned power, homogeneous_steady_states contains the rho = 1 root to machine precision. Physical constants come from scipy.constants ; no constant is typed by hand. sqzcomb.fitnoise : extraction of (mu, eta, kappa) from measured homodyne noise spectra in dB relative to shot noise -- the standard characterization of a below-threshold squeezer. fit_noise_spectra fits the package's own input-output model (the same code path as sqzcomb.spectra , cross-checked in the tests against the independent closed form) to the squeezed/antisqueezed trace pair, with an optional white dark-noise floor and per-point measurement sigmas enabling a chi-square consistency check. Identifiability is enforced, not hoped for: one quadrature alone is a single Lorentzian with two shape numbers for three unknowns, so the single-trace fit is refused unless an independently measured kappa_hz is supplied; an antisqueezed trace systematically below shot noise is refused as unphysical. Changed scipy is now a declared dependency (the new modules use scipy.constants and scipy.optimize.least_squares ). Anchors (asserted in tests/test_adapt.py , not stated) Conversion round trips exact to 1e-15; F(4P) = 2F(P); at fixed eta_esc, doubling kappa halves F. threshold_power hits the rho = 1 root of the package's own cubic for alpha in {0.7, 1.0, 1.8}. Noise-free synthetic spectra return the generating (mu, eta, kappa) to better than 1e-6; the fitted model equals the closed form S = 0.5[1 -/+ 4 eta mu / ((1 +/- mu)^2 + Omega^2)] at every frequency to 1e-10. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted parameters matches the reported one-sigma uncertainties; a dark floor deliberately omitted from the model biases eta, and fitting it recovers the truth. The under-determined single-trace case and the impossible below-shot-noise antisqueezed trace are refused with explanatory errors. Full test suite: 80 passed. See CHANGELOG.md for details.
title: sqzcomb: Lugiato-Lefever steady states and detected squeezing spectra for Kerr microcombs

summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justifiably verify from the evidence and resources available to it? This paper organizes the question around distinct boundaries of identification, generation, computation, implementation and correspondence. For a declared space of possibilities and an evidence map, exact verification is possible precisely when the demanded claim is constant on each evidence fiber. A local version characterizes sound answers at a particular observation and separates unresolved evidence from observations outside the declared model. Computation or recursive generation based solely on unchanged evidence cannot distinguish possibilities that evidence leaves indistinguishable. The paper separates semantic support from effective computation and resource-bounded attainment. In explicitly presented finite classes, it develops adaptive acquisition, relational candidate selection, safe revision composition and finite-machine attainment results under declared operational contracts. It distinguishes pointwise availability from uniform implementation and identifies conditions under which abstraction and execution preserve the guarantees being claimed. Probabilistic continuation is treated through explicit probability assumptions and attainable guarantee regions; ideal convex mixing is distinguished from mixtures realizable under hard resource limits. Contextual equivalence for declared continuation systems preserves both demanded guarantees and metadata. These results support a structured verification record that distinguishes established answers, insufficient evidence, computational exhaustion, unavailable implementations, unresolved authority and model inconsistency. The routing protocol is sound under its stated assumptions rather than a universal classification of every possible failure. The framework also separates correctness within a model from evidence that the model represents a concrete system, including the verifier itself. Its contribution is a synthesis of exact conditions, impossibility witnesses and attainable constructions that makes the boundaries of justified verification explicit without converting internal coherence, agreement or successful execution into an unsupported claim about reality.
title: The Verification Boundary: Exact Limits of Verification by Bounded Systems: Identification, Generation, Computation, Implementation, Correspondence — and the Forced Routing at Each Limit

summary: The UCT Flourish 2027 Co-Curriculum represents the second full annual cycle of an established student-facing programme developed through the Centre for Wellbeing and Flourishing at the University of Cape Town. Building directly on the 2026 cycle, the 2027 programme emphasises continuation, replication, refinement and cumulative learning rather than first-stage piloting. It is organised across five connected domains: Journey, Community, Amplify, Knowledge and Wisdom, spanning intrapsychic, interpersonal, infrastructural, interdependent and intergenerational dimensions of flourishing. The annual architecture combines a weekly VIA Character Strengths and Flourishing Seminar Series, a recurring Monthly Masterclass, two sustained 30 Days of TURN interventions, and a set of signature programmes including UCT Flourish Verse, the UCT Flourish Lab, the Student Summit and the Annual Wellbeing and Flourishing Conference. Programming is aligned with the academic calendar, public holidays, vacation periods and assessment demands, with deliberate pauses for consolidation, evaluation and research. At its centre is the question: What makes human flourishing possible? The co-curriculum creates recurring opportunities for students to develop psychological capacities, strengthen relationships, participate in university life, engage with evidence and scholarship, and contribute their own experiences and perspectives to a developing institutional conversation about flourishing. The 2027 programme remains provisional and non-exhaustive, allowing additional initiatives, partnerships and funded opportunities to be incorporated as they emerge.
title: UCT Flourish 2027: Proposed Provisional Annual Co-Curriculum

summary: Dataset Overview & Methodology This repository provides an experimentally enriched network traffic dataset designed to overcome severe class imbalance in Web attack detection . Focusing on the CICIDS2017 benchmark, which natively contains critically scarce instances for minority Web threats (such as only 21 SQL Injection flows), this dataset incorporates 32,670 authentic attack flows captured in a controlled experimental testbed . Key Characteristics Authentic Capture Environment: Unlike synthetic interpolation methods (e.g., SMOTE) that generate artificial data points within existing boundaries, this dataset captures real network traffic using an Apache XAMPP server and Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) . It features both automated scripts ( sqlmap , Hydra , Wfuzz ) and manual obfuscation vectors combined with normal background traffic . Feature-Space Consistency: Processed directly via CICFlowMeter to extract the exact 78 statistical flow features required to maintain complete compatibility with the original CICIDS2017 feature space . Rigorously Evaluated Classes: Web SQL Injection (significantly boosted to ensure robust pattern learning) . Web Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (including reflected and stored variants with filter-evasion techniques) . Web Brute Force (WBF) (generated through multi-day credential-guessing sessions) .
tags: Intrusion detection; CICIDS2017; Web attacks; Class imbalance; Traffic augmentation; LightGBM; CICFlowMeter; Multiclass classification
title: Enriched CICIDS2017 Web Attacks Dataset for Network Intrusion Detection

summary: This project investigates early training dynamics in robotic manipulation by comparing Truncated Quantile Critics (TQC), TQC with Hindsight Experience Replay (HER), and a reward-shaped TQC+HER variant in the sparse-reward FetchPickAndPlace-v4 environment. The proposed reward shaping provides intermediate signals for object contact, grasping, lifting, and moving toward the target, with all variants evaluated under matched training conditions using success rate, episode return, AUC, seed variance, and non-parametric significance testing. Results showed that baseline TQC and TQC+HER exhibited very limited early learning, while the reward-shaped variant achieved the best final performance but no statistically significant improvement, suggesting that simple hand-crafted reward shaping alone is insufficient to reliably improve early-stage learning in sparse robotic manipulation tasks.
title: Effects of Enhancing TQC with Reward Shaping on Early Training Dynamics in FetchPickAndPlace-v4

summary: Frequency-shift corrections are applied in deep-space navigation as a catalogue of formulas: common offsets, detector-end $O(c^{-3})$ cross terms and the nonlinear Doppler bias are re-derived for every mission and every data type. This paper derives the structure itself, from a single transitivity axiom. Under that axiom the endpoint factor of any light-path observable is a ratio of generators --- the \textbf{Fuxi value} $\FX_{A\|B}=\alpha_A/\alpha_B$ --- multiplied by a path factor; the generator is identified with the rate of proper-time flow, $\alpha_X=\mathrm d\tau_X/\mathrm dt_{\rm GalST}$. The resulting framework (Fuxi-ratio Mapping Theory, hereafter FMT) leaves the path-dependent transfer factor $\Pi_{\rm TTF}$ with the full complexity of the null-geodesic boundary-value problem, while its $1$PN expansion reproduces the standard frequency-shift formulas term by term at $O(c^{-2})$ and endows the IAU conversion constants $L_C,L_G,L_B$ with a direct generator interpretation. Three consequences are closed-form. \textbf{(i)} The projected pulsar-Doppler residual is \emph{exactly} linear in the relativistic velocity $\mathbf u\equiv\gamma\mathbf v$: the $O(c^{-3})$ kinematic term of the coordinate-velocity parameterization is a parameterization effect with the exact closed form $v_D^3/(2c^2)\,\hat{\mathbf v}_D$, removable in one analytic step, and \emph{identically absent} under $\mathbf u$. \textbf{(ii)} Isotropic and dipolar residual components are absorbed exactly --- the latter as a velocity error independent of the pulsar number and of the network geometry. \textbf{(iii)} Residuals of angular order $\ell\ge2$ are \emph{not} absorbed; their leakage is fixed by the higher moments of the pulsar directions, so precision and bias immunity are governed by different moments of the same network. Velocity identifiability is necessary and sufficient: the pulsar directions must not be cocircular. Model-internal consistency tests with a realistic 16-pulsar IPTA geometry reach $16.1\ \mu$m/s (three-axis RMS) at ideal timing precision $\sigma_\delta=10^{-13}$, and a full Earth-departure-to-Mars-surface arc is closed by the same expression with only its inputs changed. Both statements are model-internal limits: the term-by-term agreement with the standard formulas is limited to $O(c^{-2})$, the velocity figures presuppose an ephemeris residual $\delta C_P\lesssim3\times10^{-14}$, and practical accuracy is bounded by clock, ephemeris and direction knowledge. FMT modifies neither general relativity nor observational hardware: it is an algebraic interface callable on existing ephemerides and timing data.
title: Relativistic Doppler Velocimetry from One Transitivity Axiom: Exact Bias and Identifiability

summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. It combines internal decision state, ranking stability, external evidence, source-data provenance, and branch-specific promotion gates to emit bounded manuscript claim states, so that an exploratory signal cannot be promoted to a biological or translational conclusion without the evidence a promotion rule requires. Distribution-aware statistics (a Wasserstein statistic for full expression-distribution shifts and a histogram-shape statistic for responder-associated expression-shape changes) are retained as upstream scoring modules that supply scores to the compiler; they are not claimed as the main methodological novelty. This archive is a code-only software release and excludes manuscript drafts, submission materials, figures, source-data tables, and review materials.
title: PGAA: a claim-state compiler for perturbation-transcriptomic evidence

summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

summary: This research edition studies a concrete finite part of the Riemann zeta function's spectral data. A packet is a chosen finite collection of its zeros, with every selected multiplicity retained. Its polynomial h divides the completed function g=2xi. The original theta-function source has Mellin transform g/h. Tensor products of this source represent sums of the selected zero jets, including their full repeated-root structure. The purpose is to calculate the cost of those spectral configurations in the original arithmetic source norm. It is not to choose a favorable new metric or to assert that an off-critical-line zero exists. What to read Main research reader, 482 pages. The complete literature-and-proof synthesis now includes Section 41 on arithmetic source/relation volumes and Section 42 on gamma convolution descent. The end of Section 42 proves the direct analytic generating-function map into the same Toda input. Split-Zero/Toda companion, 424 pages. A cumulative, more focused account of the source, its cohomological quotient and finite spectral controls, with 38 proof chapters and 18 complete source appendices. The new chapters calculate the separate source and relation curvature terms, certified theta-seed inputs, and an exact Gaussian calibration. Separate full source ZIPs. These retain the mathematical texts, formalization sources and scoped checking records for each reader. Earlier published PDFs and archives remain separate downloads. Gamma and endpoint workbenches. The delivered HTML/Markdown/LaTeX argument and its finite checker remain readable separately. The endpoint criterion and its gamma-coordinate substitution explain a finite-window way to choose one of the existing canonical representatives. The attempts, their motivation and their results Exterior trace control. Why it was tried: A single-vector bound can miss the combined displacement of many spectral directions. What it establishes: The finite exterior calculation bounds their aggregate positive trace defect using the same rank-two allowance, with multiplicities and source factors retained. Source and relation volumes. Why it was tried: Relations vanish in the quotient, but their source norms still affect the least-norm representatives. What it establishes: The determinant of the canonical quotient metric is exactly a source Hankel determinant divided by a relation Hankel determinant. Two Toda flows. Why it was tried: Both determinant sequences come from exponential deformation of the original arithmetic measure. What it establishes: Their derivative formulas calculate the source/relation curvature and the original complex cross term. The finite upper estimate retains explicit nonnegative losses. Gamma convolution descent. Why it was tried: Computing a new high-dimensional convolution integral for each tensor degree is expensive. What it establishes: A classical gamma reference, multiplied by the actual arithmetic amplitude, gives an exact all-tensor coefficient formula and an explicit tail majorant. Its relative-fibre component is retained. Analytic generating-function map. Why it was tried: The coefficient expansion and the Toda moment function appeared as separate descriptions of the same source. What it establishes: They are linked by an explicit analytic map and inverse. A degree-N Gram matrix differentiated j times uses only the one-factor coefficients through degree 2N+j. Endpoint degree selection. Why it was tried: Bounding every recurrence coefficient in a whole degree window is stronger than selecting one useful canonical degree. What it establishes: The written finite Jensen argument uses four endpoint quotient volumes and two endpoint polynomial norms. The gamma-coordinate version retains the exact reference and arithmetic correction factors. The quantities are attached to explicit maps At degree N the source is the original polynomial space, mapped to the cyclic algebra C[S]/(chi). The relation columns are multiplication by the original
title: Arithmetic zeta packets: quotient volumes, Toda control and gamma convolution

summary: Experimental-workflow release: the two loose ends of the measured-data path are closed, so a squeezing estimate needs no hand-entered inputs beyond the atom number. The mean fringe obeys A cos phi + B sin phi + d exactly (the rotation law of the mean spin, no lineshape assumption), so the fit is closed-form weighted linear least squares with per-phase standard errors, and the contrast uncertainty follows by the delta method through the exact WLS covariance -- the same structure and honesty as variance_tomography . summary: Abstract Background Dapsone is a key component of multidrug therapy (MDT) for Hansen's disease but is associated with serious adverse effects, including methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and hepatotoxicity. The simultaneous occurrence of these complications is rare and potentially life-threatening. Early recognition is critical, especially in resource-limited settings where advanced diagnostic tools may not be readily available. Case Report The patient presented with jaundice, fever, and breathlessness approximately one month after initiation of dapsone therapy. Examination revealed pallor, icterus, and edema. Laboratory findings showed severe hyperbilirubinemia (>25 mg/dL), elevated transaminases, anemia (hemoglobin ~8 g/dL), markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase (1705 U/L), and negative Coombs test, consistent with non-immune hemolysis. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and arterial blood gas analysis indicated metabolic acidosis. Methemoglobinemia was clinically diagnosed by the treating team. Imaging revealed pleural effusion and ascites, suggesting systemic involvement. Dermatology consultation suggested dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome, and dapsone was discontinued. The overall findings were consistent with dapsone-induced multisystem toxicity involving hepatic, hematological, and respiratory systems. Conclusion This case highlights a rare but severe presentation of dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and acute liver failure. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for dapsone toxicity in patients presenting with jaundice, anemia, and respiratory symptoms shortly after initiation of therapy. Early drug withdrawal and prompt supportive management are essential to prevent life-threatening complications.
title: Dapsone-Induced Hemolytic Anemia, Severe Acute Liver Injury and Clinically Suspected Methemoglobinemia in a Patient with Hansen's Disease: A Rare Case Report.

summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.
title: Separating Capability from Permission in a Language Model: Prerequisite-Conditioned Native Continuation Control with Frozen Content

summary: This white paper examines decision authenticity as an emerging enterprise governance requirement in an environment where synthetic voice, video, executive likeness, and real-time presence increasingly weaken traditional signals of authority. The paper argues a meeting remains useful for discussion and judgment, but no longer provides sufficient evidence for an irreversible decision. High-risk commitments instead require structured verification of identity, authority, intent, context, independence, and evidence. The analysis uses the 2024 Arup deepfake fraud, the WPP executive impersonation attempt, and the LastPass CEO voice-cloning incident to demonstrate three distinct mechanisms. Arup shows the financial consequence of meeting-based authority. WPP shows how attackers manufacture apparent corroboration across multiple communication channels. LastPass shows how verification culture and employee interruption stop synthetic authority before irreversible action occurs. The paper introduces the Trust Compression Attack framework, describing how authority, familiarity, social proof, urgency, isolation, and irreversibility combine to compress weak trust signals into a short decision window. The paper then introduces the Decision Authenticity Stack, a six-layer operating architecture covering Identity, Authority, Intent, Context, Independence, and Evidence. Together, these frameworks move enterprise control away from perceptual verification and toward provable authorisation. The operating model separates Discussion Objects, Decision Objects, and Execution Objects so conversations provide context without automatically creating authority. Risk tiers then match stronger controls to consequence, reversibility, reach, and external impact. Critical and crisis decisions require transaction-bound approval, independent verification, separation of duties, phishing-resistant authentication, defined expiry, and durable evidence. The paper extends decision authenticity beyond human impersonation into agentic AI, where machine identity, scope, permissions, policy version, human sponsorship, and attributable execution become part of the same governance problem. The central proposition is direct: presence is not authority, fluency is not authority, and access is not authority. Enterprise authority must be explicit, bounded, independently verified, and provable.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 11 August 2026.
title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 31: The Meeting Is No Longer Evidence

summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.
title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 30: The Authenticity Tax

summary: Physics upgrade: local-oscillator phase noise, the effect that decides how much squeezing a real homodyne detector keeps. Express 21, 19047 (2013); Oelker et al., Optica 3, 682 (2016); the same quadratic form used for integrated squeezers in Dean et al., npj Nanophotonics, 2026, doi:10.1038/s44310-026-00125-5). phase_noise_squeezing_db : the same statement in the dB form labs quote. max_phase_noise : the inverse question - the largest RMS phase jitter compatible with a target detected variance - with honest refusals when the target is below the intrinsic squeezing ("cannot improve") or above the jitter-saturated midpoint ("not phase-noise-limited"). Exact limits: zero jitter reproduces the static rotation law; infinite jitter lands on (V_sq + V_anti)/2; vacuum is an exact fixed point; monotonicity in sigma. max_phase_noise round-trips through phase_noise_variance exactly, and both refusals fire. Loss and phase-noise channels commute exactly (both are affine maps with the vacuum fixed point) - asserted, not assumed. 85 tests pass on Python 3.9-3.13.

summary: This chapter explores the epistemic tensions faced by researchers, particularly those from formerly colonized countries in the Global South, caught between the demands of scientific neutrality and ethical engagement with the coloniality of knowledge. In dialogue with Critical Theory and decolonial thought, the chapter highlights epistemic resilience as a posture of resistance and reconstruction of meaning. The Haitian case study, through the heritage-based preservation of the memory of slavery, illustrates how cognitive justice can serve as a bridge between emancipatory rationality and the pluriversal horizon of decoloniality. Published as a chapter (pp. 239-257) of EDUCATORÉ. Educating and Reflecting for Resilient, Critically Aware Societies, Maria Grzegorzewska University Press, Warsaw.
title: Epistemological tensions and researcher resilience in a context of coloniality: navigating between neutrality and engagement

summary: Abstract: Livestock production is central to rural livelihoods across sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in pastoral, agro-pastoral, and smallholder farming systems. Livestock provide food, income, savings, employment, insurance against shocks, manure, and social and cultural capital. However, the contribution of livestock to household welfare depends not only on production but also on households' ability to participate effectively in livestock markets and obtain fair returns. This review synthesizes literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026, with particular attention to pastoral and smallholder systems in East Africa. The evidence shows that market infrastructure, market information, producer organizations, transport, veterinary services, financial services, value addition, and improved market governance can reduce transaction costs, increase market participation, improve producer returns, and strengthen livelihood resilience. Evidence from Ethiopia demonstrates that improved livestock market sheds can increase smallholder earnings, while evidence from northern Kenya indicates that improvements in physical and communication infrastructure have strengthened market integration. However, market participation does not automatically improve welfare. Drought, climate variability, conflict, distress sales, weak bargaining power, gender inequalities, inadequate services, and restrictions on pastoral mobility can limit or reverse livelihood gains. Informal information networks, brokers, customary institutions, and cross-border trade also remain important in connecting remote producers to markets. The review therefore argues that livestock marketing should move beyond increasing sales volumes toward resilient, inclusive, equitable, and sustainable livestock value chains. Effective interventions should integrate market infrastructure, information, producer organization, animal health, finance, value addition, climate-risk management, gender empowerment, rangeland governance, conflict management, and predictable trade regulation.
tags: Livestock marketing; Pastoral livelihoods; Smallholder farmers; Market access; Livestock value chains; Climate resilience.
title: Livestock Marketing Interventions and Livelihoods in Pastoral and Smallholder Farming Systems in Sub-Saharan and East Africa: Evidence from the Literature

summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). Sample statistics Total events: 658,241 (102,699 from 1996, 555,542 from 1997–1998) Hadronic Z → qq̄: 385,583 (2000 A LR  selection) Z → e + e − : 16,547 (2001 leptonic selection) Z → μ + μ − : 13,992 (2001 leptonic selection) Z → τ + τ − : 17,133 (2001 leptonic selection) Mean particles / event: 54.4 Mean charged particles / event: 13.4 Mean |P e |: 76.14% (1996), 73.08% (1997–1998) Simulated events (Monte Carlo) New in v3. Simulated mini-DSTs produced by the SLD collaboration's own simulation and reconstruction chain, recovered from the SLAC archives alongside the data. The sample contains 260,94
title: SLD reconstructed mini-DSTs from the 1996-1998 SLC runs and documentation corpus

summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five completions (the floor axiom, bias as signal, the developmental axis, self-propagation, and the translation function) and seven operators (grounding defaults, reframes, win-win-win incentives, developmental pricing, regulation rituals, lateral social proof, and the door) specify the discipline as buildable rather than rhetorical. The research program states the core hypothesis in falsifiable form: bias magnitudes measured in the classical paradigms are partly substrate-dependent and will shift under floor restoration, tested against an active control using canonical instruments. The measurement problem is stated rather than finessed — there is no clean control group, because there is no reservoir of reliably grounded subjects and therefore no true zero — with within-subject designs, natural experiments, and dose-response gradients offered as partial routes. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. Companion to the five-essay Spine. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.
title: Luminous Behavioral Economics: The Translation Layer Between the Floor and the Civilization

summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. summary: Essay Five of the Spine, and its last. Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.
title: The Noosphere: The Holon That Comes Next

summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).
tags: LLM agents; cyber deception; network security
title: Four-Run Lab Containment of an AutoGen and GPT-4o Attack Agent Under Production Automated Moving Target Defense: Method, Logs, and Limits
