summary: This paper proves four independent conditions under which a system's perceived state can become detached from its true state, and shows what follows when that detachment coincides with self-reinforcing dynamics that make an eventual correction harder to reverse than it was to prevent. A sequence of individually imperceptible changes can accumulate to arbitrary cumulative drift without any single step ever being flagged. Two independent, fully rational reasons can lead a corrective judgment to be legitimately suspended: genuine uncertainty about the reliability of one's own instrument, and a collapse of verification incentive below a sharp cost threshold. Even a fully active, fully resourced, fully self-trusting corrector faces a hard information-theoretic ceiling on accuracy once the signal distinguishing genuine change from ordinary variation grows statistically indistinguishable. A population state governed by a bandwagon-reinforced dynamic exhibits a trichotomy of long-run outcomes separated by a hysteresis gap, so reversing an already-shifted state requires strictly more than what triggered the shift. Together, these results suggest a precise reading of familiar worries about smartphone habits, synthetic media, and self-reinforcing online communities, not as vague metaphors, but as specific, checkable conditions under which an unnoticed and hard-to-reverse drift becomes possible.
title: Correction Freeze Problem

summary: English — Abstract U = Δ develops an operational-relational framework that takes difference, rather than objects, substances, space, time, or motion, as the minimal condition from which a finite description of a physical world can be constructed. The starting expression U=ΔU=\Delta is progressively developed through a finite observational window W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , which determines the spatial and temporal resolution at which differences can be distinguished. Differences below that resolution are compressed, while the resolved field is represented through successive saturations. Within each saturation, relatively stable regions are treated as conventions rather than absolute entities. Every convention is defined together with its complement and acquires an operational boundary. Persistence is then reconstructed not as immobility or intrinsic identity, but as a history of reconfirmations across successive readings under the same window. Relative persistence, local spatiotemporal comparison, boundary redrawing, deformation, movement, emergence and disappearance are developed from this common relational structure. The dynamical part of the work studies evolution as a recursive process of local reattribution between successive saturations. A resolved convention can retain the same macroscopic extension while undergoing non-zero internal turnover; consequently, stability does not imply absence of process. Incoming and outgoing reattributions are treated as complementary descriptions of the same local transitions, while coherent patterns of reattribution can give rise to macroscopic notions such as motion and flow rather than requiring them as primitive variables. The remaining development investigates the minimal mathematical closure of this recursive evolution, the reconstruction of changing adjacency and boundary networks, the effect of changing observational windows and resolution scales, and the conditions under which the resulting framework can support quantitative prediction and empirical falsification. Particular attention is given to distinguishing logical consequences, operational definitions, scale-dependent descriptions, and constitutive or empirical laws that must be independently calibrated. The aim is therefore not to replace established physical theories with an assumed microscopic ontology, but to investigate a minimal grammar through which resolved objects, persistence, boundaries, dynamics and continuity may emerge from recursively organized difference. Italiano — Abstract U = Δ sviluppa un quadro operativo-relazionale che assume la differenza, anziché oggetti, sostanze, spazio, tempo o movimento, come condizione minima dalla quale costruire una descrizione finita del mondo fisico. L’espressione iniziale U=ΔU=\Delta viene sviluppata attraverso una finestra osservativa finita W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , che determina la risoluzione spaziale e temporale alla quale le differenze possono essere distinte. Le differenze sottosoglia vengono compresse, mentre il campo risolto viene rappresentato attraverso saturazioni successive. All’interno di ogni saturazione, le regioni relativamente stabili vengono trattate come convenzioni e non come entità assolute. Ogni convenzione è definita insieme al proprio complemento e acquisisce un bordo operativo. La persistenza viene quindi ricostruita non come immobilità o identità intrinseca, ma come storia di riconferme attraverso letture successive effettuate sotto la stessa finestra. Persistenza relazionale, confronto spazio-temporale locale, ridisegno dei bordi, deformazione, movimento, emergenza e scomparsa vengono sviluppati a partire dalla stessa struttura relazionale. La parte dinamica studia l’evoluzione come processo ricorsivo di riattribuzione locale fra saturazioni successive. Una convenzione risolta può conservare la stessa estensione macroscopica
title: OPEN TO COLLABORATION, IMPORTANT - READ AND SPREAD - THEORY OF EVERYTHING - Relative Sampling and Continuous Reconventioning - Campionamento Relativo e Riconvenzionamento Continuo

summary: This repository contains the code and data used to prepare a manuscript titled "Flow dependence of boundary-layer scheme parameters revealed by stochastic inversion".  Code: The data were produced with two different ideal cases of the Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF): (1) WRFlux v1.7.0 in large-eddy simulation (LES) configuration, available at https://github.com/matzegoebel/WRFlux/ and (2) WRF v4.4.2 in single-column model configuration ( https://github.com/wrf-model/WRF/releases/tag/v4.4.2 ).  The LES and SCM simulations represent the evolution of a convective boundary layer in the atmosphere over flat terrain. To reproduce the LES simulation, download WRFlux v1.7.0 from the link above, compile as usual and run it using the namelist file and input sounding provided in LES.zip.  To reproduce the deterministic SCM simulations, a modified version of WRF v4.4.2 is needed. Download WRF v4.4.2 and replace the corresponding files with those provided in this repository under WRF_SCM.zip, then compile as usual. These modifications allow for variable parameters in the YSU planetary boundary layer (PBL) scheme instead of prescribed constant ones. The parameter values are controlled via the namelist: ysu_pfactor ( p ), ysu_bfactor ( b ), and ysu_entrainment_hfx_mag ( Ae ). WRF_SCM.zip also contains the namelist file, input sounding, and surface forcing file (scmflx_bdy) needed to run the simulation. The input sounding and scmflx_bdy files are the same for all SCM runs. To reproduce the ensemble of SCM simulations, the modified version of WRF coupled with a modified version of DART-WRF v2024.2.20 ( https://github.com/lkugler/DART-WRF/releases/tag/v2024.2.20 ) is needed. Here, DART-WRF is used only to generate an ensemble of forecasts. Download DART-WRF v2024.2.20 and copy the files provided in DART-WRF_SCM.zip into the matching paths of the DART-WRF source tree, overwriting the originals. DART-WRF_SCM.zip also contains the parameter perturbation files needed to run the large ensembles (as .txt files). The large ensembles are subject to parameter perturbations only. For further details on all simulations, please refer to the manuscript. Data: LES.zip: contains the WRFlux output (instout_d01_2001-06-05_07_00_00_compressed.nc) from which synthetic observations are drawn in this study. SCM_deterministic.zip: contains all deterministic SCM runs.  wrfout_d01_2001-06-05_07:00:00.nc: SCM output with original prescribed parameter values (see manuscript). SINGLE_PARAMETER_PERTURBATION_EXP: contains directories for each parameter with varying parameter values (still deterministic runs), e.g., in Ae_0.0 parameter Ae is set to 0 and the other two parameters remain at their prescribed values. SCM_ensemble.zip: contains all SCM ensemble runs produced with the modified version of WRF via DART-WRF. P_B_AE_C1_ensemble_27000_5min.nc: large ensemble simulation (N=27 000) with parameter perturbations for all three YSU parameters (parameter perturbation files in DART-WRF_SCM.zip), output every 5 minutes. This file is the raw ensemble from which all posterior distributions below are derived. P_C1_ensemble_N10000.nc: large ensemble simulation (N=10 000) with parameter perturbations for parameter  p only. POSTERIOR_MARGINAL_DISTRIBUTIONS: contains time dependent marginal posterior distributions as a function of each parameter (e.g., MARGINAL_Ae.npy) and their respective bins (e.g., MARGINAL_Ae_bins.npy). The algorithm to compute marginal posterior distributions can be found in the Jupyter notebook "Postprocessing.ipynb". title: Code and data for "Flow dependence of boundary-layer scheme parameters revealed by stochastic inversion"

summary: The Empirical-Axiomatic Framework (EAF) is a broader foundational framework concerned with existence, ontological structure, consistency, logic, information, representation, knowledge, scientific modelling, consciousness, and related philosophical questions. This paper develops the epistemological part of EAF by establishing a conceptual relation between underlying structures, representations, information, self, epistemic architecture, epistemic capacity, and knowledge. The paper distinguishes the Universal Information Space from the Ontological Information Space and defines knowledge as information possessed by a self, where a self is understood as a well-defined system. It further distinguishes generalised knowledge from Traditional Knowledge, with Traditional Knowledge requiring comprehended structural correspondence between a representation and the underlying structure it represents. The paper analyses epistemic activities, knowledge generation, representation changes, generator bases, and the limitations of epistemic systems. It distinguishes incomplete representations from incorrect representations and epistemic limitations from ontological limitations. A computer is examined as a detailed example of a non-biological epistemic system capable of acquiring, storing, processing, transforming, representing, and communicating information without these capacities necessarily implying consciousness or Traditional Knowledge. The framework is then applied to major epistemological and related philosophical problems, including induction, Gödel’s incompleteness problem, material implication, the philosophy of mathematics, Benacerraf’s problem, Gettier’s problem, demarcation, the Münchhausen trilemma, Sorites, and universals. The paper does not claim to provide final solutions to all these problems. Rather, it offers a unified conceptual basis for reframing them through the relations among existence, structure, representation, information, and epistemic systems. The resulting framework provides a foundation for further formal, scientific, and philosophical development within EAF.
title: Epistemology within the Empirical-Axiomatic Framework

summary: Predictive maintenance has become one of the most important approaches for improving reliability, efficiency, and operational continuity in modern industrial enterprises. Unlike corrective maintenance, which is performed after equipment failure, and preventive maintenance, which follows predetermined schedules, predictive maintenance relies on real-time condition monitoring and data analysis to estimate the probability of future faults. The aim of this study was to analyze modern predictive maintenance methods used for industrial machinery and equipment and to evaluate their advantages, limitations, and practical applications. A literature-based analytical approach was used to examine vibration analysis, temperature monitoring, acoustic emission, oil analysis, electrical signature analysis, Internet of Things technologies, machine learning, digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based diagnostic systems. The analysis indicates that combining sensor-based monitoring with intelligent data analytics can identify abnormal equipment behavior before catastrophic failure occurs. Predictive maintenance can reduce unplanned downtime, optimize spare-parts management, extend equipment life, and decrease maintenance costs. However, successful implementation depends on sensor reliability, data quality, appropriate algorithms, integration with industrial control systems, and qualified personnel. Predictive maintenance should therefore be considered a key component of smart manufacturing and modern industrial asset management.
tags: predictive maintenance, industrial machinery, condition monitoring, machine learning, vibration analysis, IoT, digital twin, equipment reliability.
title: INTELLIGENT PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE TECHNOLOGIES FOR MODERN INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22734670 . What the paper claims This is an evidence map of 11,628 PubMed-indexed records on generative language models in healthcare, January 2023 to June 2026, built to answer one question: is the clinical literature keeping pace with the systems it evaluates? The central construct is evaluation lag, the number of quarters between the release of the newest model family a study names and that study's own publication quarter. Mean lag widens from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters. Because a discontinued family ages at exactly one quarter per quarter, the authors benchmark that rise against a counterfactual holding 2023 model composition fixed, and find that migration to newer systems offsets 56.2% of the drift (95% CI 49.9-65.2, 2,000 bootstrap resamples). By design, randomised controlled trials evaluate models 4.62 quarters older than other empirical designs (95% CI 3.62-5.63), yet among the records naming a family still receiving releases no design differs from any other; what separates designs is the probability of studying a discontinued family at all, 62.1% for randomised trials against 15.6% for preprints. The framing is right and the execution is unusually careful for a bibliometric paper. Reporting the mechanical ageing rate as the null instead of zero, validating the decomposition by showing that discontinued-only records widen at 1.062 quarters per quarter, and running a pessimistic sensitivity analysis that assumes the earliest release of every named family are all things this literature normally omits. The version-specification result in Section 2 deserves to be read on its own: randomised trials specify the model version in 50.0% of cases, the lowest of any empirical design, which means half of the highest-tier evidence cannot be attributed to a determinate system. My comments below are about three places where the reported precision outruns the design. Does the conclusion hold on the data? 1. Evaluation lag is measured on a differentially selected half of the corpus, and the headline comparison is between designs that differ in exactly that selection. Lag is computable for 5,775 of 11,628 records, and coverage by design runs from 87.0% for comparative evaluations and 69.0% for randomised trials down to 36.2% for preprints and 27.0% for reviews. The paper states this plainly, which is to its credit, but the between-design contrast is its central result and the missingness is both large and design-dependent. The direction is not obvious either: if preprints name a model in the abstract mainly when that model is the novelty on sale, the preprint advantage is inflated; if trials omit the name when the system is an incidental component, the trial penalty may be understated. Two things would settle it. Worst-case bounds in the Manski sense across the plausible range would show whether the ordering survives at all, and a full-text audit of a random sample, a few hundred records stratified by design, would give an empirical estimate of how the non-naming records differ. Without one of those, the contrast rests on an assumption of ignorable missingness that the paper does not state. 2. The abstract quotes the specification that maximises the effect and omits the one that does not survive correction. The median regression gives 4.62 quarters at P = 3.4 x 10^-19; ordinary least squares on the same specification gives an adjusted difference of 1.57 quarters, P = 0.021, and after Holm correction across the seven design contrasts P = 0.084. Median regression is the defensible choice for a strongly right-skewed distribution and the paper says so, so this is not a case of specification shopping. It is a case of a reader meeting one number and not the other. The magnitude differs by a factor of about three between estimators, and the abstract should carry that range, or at minimum state that the estimate
title: PREreview of "The widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research 2023 to 2026"

summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. Patch 3.1.1: the co-activation of a named window is read on the uncut r
title: emgteach: an open-source teaching platform for surface electromyography

summary: Abstract Fungi are an ecologically diverse and important kingdom of life because of their roles in ecosystems. Current studies show that this kingdom remains underexplored and that much of its diversity is still unknown. Moreover, fungi contribute to several aspects of our well-being. They are used in the food and cosmetic industries as additives; they are found in fermented foods and beverages; and they have been used for ages in traditional Chinese medicine. The most important role is to serve in agriculture as biocontrol agents, nematicides derived from fungi, and drugs such as antibacterials, antimycotics, immunosuppressants, and cardiovascular drugs that are in use or derived from fungi.  Nevertheless, one major problem we face worldwide is the rising number of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria, fungi, and fungus-like organisms. Therefore, there is an urgent need for new drugs with a novel structure and perhaps a new mode of action to address this problem. One way to find new drugs is to explore more natural products, because around 50 percent of the drugs on the market are natural products or are somehow derived from them. Fungi play an interesting role in this because, as mentioned, they are underexplored. For a reason, it is easy to find unexplored biodiversity, together with unexplored chemical diversity. Studying fungi from less exploited taxa, geographic regions, and ecological niches can improve success. Proper identification of fungal species using a modern polyphasic approach will also help study new or interesting, not-so-well-studied taxa. Moreover, insight into biosynthetic gene clusters can provide an overview of an organism's capacity. Several different approaches are needed to activate the BCGs, which are silent under laboratory conditions. The use of different media, co-cultivation, or even genetic manipulation could be helpful. This thesis demonstrates the potential of diverse ecological environments and neglected habitats, such as dung, for identifying new fungi and natural products. Moreover, the thesis provides insight into the heterologous expression of natural products from the basidiomycete Cyclocybe aegerita , to investigate its terpene biosynthesis. Two fungi from different environmental regions: one is from a tree in a forest in Thailand, and the other was isolated from soil in Hong Kong, were investigated for their secondary metabolites. The fungus from Thailand was identified as Resupinatus sp., and the soil-borne fungus is the ascomycete Morinagamyces vermucularis . Both strains yielded several new natural products that showed activity in our in-house test panel. This could give them a potential application within different fields. With the heterologous expression of the Agr2 terpene synthase from Cyclocybe agerita , we could identify a bifunctional terpene synthase that gives rise to both a new diterpene and the known sesquiterpene viridiflorene. This first result can provide knowledge to continue identifying the diverse terpene biosynthesis in Basidiomycota. In the last part of the thesis, coprophilous fungi isolated from herbivorous dung samples collected in northern Germany were isolated and investigated. Our research led to the discovery of a new species of Parascedosporium and a new species of Scytalidium , as well as an updated description of two Collariella species. In conclusion, this study highlights the great capacity still hidden in the fungal kingdom, in both its biodiversity and its secondary metabolites. Moreover, the thesis findings are part of addressing global problems such as biodiversity loss, antibiotic resistance, and antifungal resistance.
title: Exploring Fungal Natural Product Diversity Through Integrative Taxonomy, Metabolomics, and Biosynthetic Investigation

summary: What two millennia of transmitting a canon with no living author, no writing and an active schism left behind — seven copy-integrity mechanisms with engineering forms, offered to any retrieval system that must hand a machine reader something checkable; and the finding that what the transmission left was divergence made detectable, never divergence prevented. A retrieval system that serves text to a machine reader has a problem the machine reader cannot solve for itself: the reader cannot tell a faithful copy from a plausible one. Provenance-Carrying Retrieval argued that the response should therefore carry the means of its own falsification — a hash, an independent time anchor, a citable identifier — and that the trust burden should be inverted, so that a server ships the tools to disbelieve it. This paper asks a different and prior question. Has anything ever actually run this problem to completion? One thing has, and it is not a computer system. The Theravāda Pāli canon was transmitted for roughly four centuries with no written copy at all, and for roughly two millennia in total, without a living author to arbitrate, across schism — on the Sri Lankan chronicles' account, one that produced a rival recital — through famine, war, and the ordinary attrition of the human beings who were the storage medium. That is a copy-integrity problem under a threat model that overlaps a retrieval server's without being the same one (§7 partitions the two), sustained for a duration no production system has approached. It converged on an apparatus, and this paper reads seven of its parts as engineering. All seven are transpositions, and the paper says so plainly. Five transpose practices the archival and transparency-log communities already know under other names: an inline attribution formula opening the text rather than a metadata field (§4.1); admission decided at build time by a named assembly under a recorded procedure rather than by a query-time filter (§4.2); commentary labelled as a distinct text class , from which a server inherits an obligation never to substitute generated summary for source (§4.3); variant readings preserved with their line of transmission attached rather than normalised to a preferred text (§4.4); and abridgement announced inline at the point of the cut (§4.5). Two more transpose practices known in other fields: interpretive standing carried per passage rather than per document, because an excerpt loses its document's front matter at retrieval (§4.6); and scheduled public re-verification before an assembly in which silence is a positive assertion for which the silent party is accountable (§4.7). An eighth item is a convention rather than a mechanism — every exclusion served with the case that occasioned it (§4.8). Two further designs (§5) are carried furthest from where the destination field keeps them. The conformance endpoint (§5.1) accepts a claimed quotation and returns a disposition on the claim , together with the procedure to follow next, and by construction returns no disposition on the claimant — the part a hash does not have, because a hash reports that a comparison failed and says nothing about what to do. It is offered as a new composition: closed disposition sets about a submitted object are old (OCSP), and what is new is a set over a multi-recension corpus that includes a conforming variant with its witness. The separated completeness manifest (§5.2) is a signed, versioned and expiring statement of a collection's membership and cardinality published as an artifact distinct from the index it describes, on the ground that an index cannot attest to its own completeness : a silently dropped document is invisible to every check that reads the index, and detectable to a third party holding only the manifest. It is a transposition, with The Update Framework's snapshot and timestamp metadata and BagIt's Payload-Oxum as its nearest prior art. The paper's most important result is a narrowing, and it is stated
title: The Reciters' Protocol

summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .
title: The Cost of Reliability in Optimal Magnetization Switching: A Longitudinal-Field Front for Van der Waals Magnets

summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.
tags: Parkinson's disease; voice analysis; machine learning; reproducibility; data leakage; class imbalance; cross-dataset validation; external validity; digital biomarkers
title: Evaluation Design, Class Imbalance, and Cross-Dataset Generalisation in Voice-Based Parkinson's Disease Detection: A Reproducibility Report

summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. summary: The paper addresses an ambiguity in chaos diagnostics. A positive Lyapunov exponent establishes local instability and the failure of exact point prediction, but it does not show whether chaotic motion can carry a system across the boundary that defines operational failure. The authors distinguish thin chaos, where local instability remains confined, from thick chaos, where chaotic transport becomes failure-relevant, with transitional chaos as the warning regime between them. To make this distinction operational, they introduce the thinness index, which compares the amount of chaotic transport in a coherence-relevant variable over a chosen timescale with the displacement required to reach failure. The paper develops a step-by-step protocol: define an operational timescale, measure local instability, identify a coherent region, choose a transport variable, estimate chaotic transport, define a failure scale, compute the index, assess uncertainty, and interpret the result. Three applications illustrate the approach. A MEMS resonator shows how chaotic amplitude fluctuations can remain well below the pull-in margin. A celestial Trojan system shows how chaotic libration need not imply escape over a given horizon. A mode-locked laser shows how phase jitter can remain within locking tolerance despite local chaos. In each case, the index distinguishes harmless local irregularity from transport that threatens function. The paper stresses several benefits. The index is quantitative, interpretable as the fraction of the failure margin consumed by chaos, timescale-relative, function-relative, comparative across domains, and useful for early warning and control. It does not replace Lyapunov exponents or transport theory but complements them. The limitations are explicit: the index depends on the chosen coherent region, failure boundary, transport variable, and timescale. It measures scale but not topology, and uncertainty matters near the transition. The conclusion is that chaos becomes dangerous not when it appears but when it connects. This offers a precise operational language for scientists and engineers.
title: The Thinness Index: A Transport-Based Diagnostic for Chaos in Engineered and Natural Systems

summary: Introduction: Carpal tunnel release is highly effective; however, a subset of patients develops persistent or recurrent symptoms requiring revision surgery. Failure may reflect incomplete decompression, perineural scarring, technical injury, or patient-related systemic and occupational factors. This study aimed to assess the incidence of revision surgery and identify its independent predictors following primary carpal tunnel release. Material and methods: This retrospective, descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Imam Reza Hospital, Tabriz, Iran, and included 300 adults who underwent primary carpal tunnel release. Eligible records were selected through convenience sampling. Demographic, clinical, electrophysiological, surgical, postoperative, and revision-related data were extracted from medical records using a standardized form and analyzed statistically to determine the incidence and predictors of revision surgery. Results: Revision carpal tunnel surgery occurred in 8.0% of patients. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative severe electrodiagnostic grade (adjusted OR=3.86, 95% CI:1.31-11.38; P=0.014), persistent postoperative pillar or scar pain (adjusted OR=3.41, 95% CI:1.18-9.85; P=0.023), primary endoscopic release (adjusted OR=3.25, 95% CI:1.04-10.15; P=0.043), preoperative thenar atrophy (adjusted OR=3.12, 95% CI:1.08-8.99; P=0.035), and diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR=2.94, 95% CI:1.05-8.24; P=0.040) as independent predictors of revision surgery. Conclusion: Secondary revision following carpal tunnel release is primarily driven by advanced baseline neural degeneration, metabolic comorbidity, endoscopic decompression, and persistent postoperative pillar pain. Comprehensive preoperative electrodiagnostic risk stratification, careful surgical technique selection, and targeted glycemic management are essential to mitigate surgical failure rates and optimize long-term clinical recovery.
title: Assessment of the Incidence and Predictors of Revision Surgery Following Carpal Tunnel Release

summary: Physical theories have been highly successful in analysing phenomena associated with motion, such as forces, trajectories, fields, and spacetime dynamics, yet comparatively little attention has been given to motion itself as a foundational problem. Across classical mechanics, quantum theory, and general relativity, motion is treated as a presupposed background condition rather than as an entity requiring ontological grounding. This paper identifies this asymmetry as a neglected issue in the foundations of physics. By examining the conceptual role of physical laws across major theoretical frameworks, it is argued that such laws constrain the form of motion without accounting for its persistent existence. This reveals a limitation common to inert ontological assumptions, according to which matter and fields lack the intrinsic capacity to sustain dynamical activity. The paper, therefore, addresses the ontic foundations of physical law alongside the problem of motion itself. To this end, the Kinetic Ground Hypothesis is introduced as a prescriptive interpretive model in which motion is understood as requiring continuous sustaining conditions rather than inertial self-maintenance. Within this framework, physical laws are reinterpreted as stable abstractions of an underlying nomological order. The grounding of motion and law is connected to consciousness through a novel model, distinct from standard fine-tuning and nomological harmony approaches, and informed by Indian philosophical metaphysics. Without altering empirical physics, the study offers an ontological clarification relevant to both foundational physics and contemporary metaphysical debate.
title: The Kinetic Ground Hypothesis: Addressing the Problem of Motion through Vedic Nomology

summary: The present study characterised the environmental status of Tortugas Bay (Casma, Peru) by integrating biological indices with physicochemical variables, drawing on analyses of subtidal macrobenthic assemblages and water-column conditions. Sam-pling was undertaken at six stations spanning a gradient of anthropogenic pressure across three contrasting seasonal periods in 2023; sediments and benthic macrofauna were collected using a Van Veen grab and processed according to standardised pro-tocols. Biodiversity metrics (species richness and abundance, together with Shannon, Simpson, Pielou and Margalef indices) were computed, and multivariate approaches (PCA, nMDS and PERMANOVA) were employed. The results indicated a pronounced spatial gradient of sediment organic enrichment, peaking at station E-01 (5.20 ± 0.32%) and reaching a minimum at E-06 (1.70 ± 0.50%), with an inverse association to water transparency (1.77 ± 0.23 m at E-01 versus 3.10 ± 0.27 m at E-04). Principal component analysis accounted for 57% of the overall environmental variability and identified sediment organic matter as the dominant structuring driver. Stations subject to greater organic enrichment displayed elevated abundances (up to 512 individuals) alongside reduced diversity (H′ = 2.00) and evenness (J′ = 0.67), whereas comparatively open and better-flushed stations supported assemblages that were both more diverse and more evenly distributed (H′ up to 2.50). Collectively, the integrated use of biological indices and multivariate analyses yielded a robust appraisal of the bay’s environmental con-dition and established a sound baseline for long-term monitoring and sustainable management.
title: BIOLOGICAL INDICES TO CHARACTERIZE THE ENVIRONMENTAL STATE OF A MARINE ECOSYSTEM SUBJECTED TO ANTHROPOGENIC PRESSURE

summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.32. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial knot type is at least 6.32. The proof combines an acyclic essential-secant bootstrap, exact compatible affine radial transfers, covered joint-radius propagation, exact profile convolution, ordered failure boundaries, and retained distortion constraints through a common interior knot point. The complete computer-assisted certificate chain was run independently at 96-bit and 192-bit precision; each run certified 2,024,886 boxes across 52 sequential stages and 132 uniform regional results, with all 26 verification-source hashes frozen. This record contains the 19-page version 1.0 preprint and its complete reproducible source and verification package. The preprint has not been submitted to or accepted by a journal.

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22737224 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes It explains the problem properly, namely the need for reliable methods for miRNA analysis, as RNA-seq methods are not able to account for its specific characteristics. It also points out the gaps in prior benchmarking studies, clearly identifying that a benchmark particularly for normalization and differential expression has not been performed before, especially one incorporating recently developed methods. Lastly, it clearly states its aim and overall approach. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate 1. Some methodological details are missing. PCA and heatmap figures (figure 1B and 1C) are presented in Results alone, with no explanation in Methods section. So no information on the input data (raw or normalized or log), if it was scaled, the miRNAs selection criteria, or what clustering methods were applied. Due to this, the reproducibility of the paper is affected. 2. The paper frames as evaluating a broad range of normalization strategies but just tests only two types: within-sample scaling (RPM, RPM_total, MAP) and cross-sample (DESeq2,TMM). Other options such as quantile normalization or compositional data methods were not tested. 3. An uneven comparison in the differential expression benchmark, two different input data types used. Most methods use miRNA-level count matrix whereas miRglmm uses isomiR-level count matrix. Still, the authors do not address whether miRglmm's strong performance is due to the model or input data. 4. The underlying logic for the ground truth is circular. The authors state that DE ground truth is defined by "monotonicity trends derived from RPM values". But RPM is what they recommend for normalization. So ranking other tools against a baseline that uses their preferred method creates a feedback loop that is not validated against any independent benchmark. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported 1. The paper relies almost entirely on monotonicity as the ground-truth signal, across normalization, differential expression and log2FC tissue-specificity direction. While its limitations are acknowledged, its recommendations seem overconfident due to the narrow validation scope and too much reliance on a single criterion. 2. The authors identified pancreatic contamination in Mouse 3, clearly separating on PC2. summary: Martin Scorsese’s 1991 Cape Fear is often remembered as a violent psychological thriller built around Robert De Niro’s grotesque performance as Max Cady, but the film’s deeper force lies in its study of guilt, moral contamination, family breakdown, adolescent vulnerability, and the collapse of legal authority. A remake of J. Lee Thompson’s 1962 film, itself adapted from John D. MacDonald’s novel The Executioners, Scorsese’s version shifts the moral center of the story. In the original, Max Cady largely functions as an external predator who invades the life of a fundamentally decent lawyer and his family. In the 1991 version, Cady becomes something more disturbing: the return of Sam Bowden’s repressed guilt, the embodiment of a legal and moral failure that cannot remain buried. This essay argues that Scorsese’s Cape Fear is not merely a story about a family stalked by a criminal. It is a film about the psychological collapse of respectability under pressure. Through Max Cady, Sam Bowden, Leigh Bowden, Danielle Bowden, Lori Davis, and the compromised figures of law surrounding them, Scorsese turns a home-invasion thriller into a fevered southern-gothic nightmare about guilt, sexuality, punishment, and the terrifying instability of civilized identity.
title: The Return of the Repressed: Family Guilt, Moral Contamination and the Psychological Terror of Scorsese's Cape Fear

summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justify from its evidence, computation and memory, and what follows when those resources cannot settle its question? This paper develops a mathematical account of verification boundaries under explicit task, evidence and resource contracts. An evidence-based verifier cannot correctly decide a claim that takes different truth values within one evidence fiber. Generating hypotheses or recursively processing the same evidence does not remove that obstruction without an additional informative channel or premise. Related results separate semantic determination, effective computation and bounded implementation; show why some finite resource classes have incomparable attainable capabilities rather than one greatest evaluator; and characterize conditional limits on self-verification. Positive results complement these obstructions. Finite query-tree constructions characterize adaptive acquisition and relational answer selection under declared costs. Explicit finite-machine models provide attainable implementation families with accounted resources and transport bounds. For finite permitted procedure classes, maximal antichains characterize terminal guarantee feasibility; their limitations under continuation distinguish terminal comparison from compositional preservation. Probability is treated through separate objects: posterior belief, environmental stochastic assumptions and private algorithmic randomization. Failure of a deterministic guarantee supplies no premise-free probability estimate. The results support a typed verification protocol: accepted certificates justify scoped assertions, bounded dispatch returns unresolved outcomes when necessary, and multiple obstruction causes remain visible beneath any summary label. Soundness, termination, diagnostic completeness and implementation correspondence are separate obligations. The paper establishes conditional boundaries and attainable constructions for its specified classes, while leaving general model correspondence and unrestricted justified self-improvement as distinct questions. This public edition updates the previously deposited v6.3 release. It corrects editorial status and import-scope wording, clarifies that probabilistic continuation requires additional declared premises, and incorporates the reference correction. Mathematical statements and proofs are preserved. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.
title: The Verification Boundary: Exact Limits of Verification by Bounded Systems: Identification, Generation, Computation, Implementation, Correspondence — and the Forced Routing at Each Limit

summary: The IMEB-Exo Synthetic Benchmark Dataset is an open and reproducible dataset developed for the analysis of passive upper-limb exoskeletons, occupational biomechanics, human–exoskeleton interaction, and multicriteria biomechanical decision support. It provides deterministic synthetic time-series data and derived biomechanical indicators designed to support methodological validation, sensitivity analysis, benchmarking, and reproducibility of the IMEB-Exo framework (Multicriteria Biomechanical Exposure Index for Exoskeletons). The dataset represents 24 virtual anthropometric models evaluated under three simulated occupational task scenarios and two experimental conditions: without exoskeleton assistance and with a passive upper-limb exoskeleton. The data structure enables comparisons between assisted and non-assisted conditions across multiple anthropometric profiles, task scenarios, and human–exoskeleton interface regions. The time-series dataset includes normal and tangential human–exoskeleton interface forces, estimated interface pressure when a technically defined contact area is available, shoulder and trunk kinematics, exoskeleton assistance torque, joint reaction variables, muscle activation surrogates, and cumulative biomechanical exposure indicators. Derived variables include peak and mean force, 95th-percentile force, root mean square (RMS) force, force–time integral, loading rate, time above an operational load threshold, peak counts, projected occupational exposure, CRITIC objective weights, TOPSIS results, IMEB-Exo scores, biomechanical criticality classes (CCB-Exo), and rankings of human–exoskeleton interface regions. The repository contains: • deterministic synthetic biomechanical time-series data; • interface-level and scenario-level metrics; • IMEB-Exo scores and regional rankings; • CRITIC objective weights and TOPSIS outputs; • metadata for 24 virtual anthropometric models; • task and scenario definitions; • human–exoskeleton interface definitions and contact-area specifications; • generation parameters; • a structured SQLite database; • CSV and compressed CSV datasets; • Python scripts for dataset generation and IMEB-Exo calculation; • data dictionary and schema documentation; • SHA-256 checksums and file inventory; • representative figures and data excerpts; • reproducibility documentation in English and Portuguese. The dataset is intended for researchers working with occupational biomechanics, passive occupational exoskeletons, wearable robotics, ergonomic risk assessment, musculoskeletal modelling, multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA/MCDM), decision-support systems, synthetic biomechanical datasets, and reproducible computational research. Methodological notice: the dataset is synthetic and deterministic. The generated variables reproduce the expected structure and behaviour of an OpenSim-oriented musculoskeletal simulation workflow but do not constitute experimentally measured human data and must not be interpreted as direct outputs from an executed OpenSim simulation. The dataset should therefore be used as a methodological benchmark for algorithm development, reproducibility testing, sensitivity analysis, multicriteria modelling, and computational workflow validation rather than as experimental evidence of human biomechanical responses. The dataset was developed within the project “Multicriteria Methods for the Analysis of Monitored Data in the Use of Passive Upper-Limb Exoskeletons”, supported by FAEPEX / University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Grant No. 70262-26.
title: IMEB-Exo Synthetic Dataset: Time-Series Biomechanical Data and Multicriteria Indicators for Passive Upper-Limb Exoskeleton Assessment

summary: Clarifying dialogue can supply evidence about another person's interpretation while changing the interpretation being investigated. This paper develops a relational-history account of the resulting inference problem. It separates current coordination, retrospective attribution, and the prospective formation of understanding, while treating relations, histories, interpretive conditions, and response profiles as jointly constrained. A finite model retains paired initial and current candidate states through inquiry-induced transitions. Exact recovery of an earlier target requires constancy across the initial histories compatible with the complete dialogue transcript. A bounded adaptive-inquiry recursion characterizes when an allowed sequence of questions can achieve that recovery, and a constructive example shows how successful explanation can erase the discriminating opportunity while securing present mastery. Further examples distinguish historical ambiguity, response ambiguity, contextual error, and participants' interpretations of an investigator's expectations. The philosophical analysis connects first-person authority, interpersonal understanding, and the formation of shared meaning without identifying predictive success with access to another person's experience. A proposed study separates immediate correct responding, transfer, and retrospective attribution. The results are conditional formal consequences and conceptual distinctions; their psychological adequacy and the comparative merits of the proposed inquiry procedure remain empirical questions.
title: Theory of Mind in Clarifying Dialogue: Inferring Another Person's Interpretation from Relational History

summary: This white paper examines the operational, financial, customer, governance, and leadership consequences arising when customer-facing artificial intelligence makes a commitment the enterprise did not intend to make. The central argument is that a machine-generated promise becomes an enterprise risk when a customer reasonably relies on the output or when organisational systems allow the machine to act on it. The resulting exposure extends beyond hallucination into authority, workflow, customer reliance, execution, redress, and accountability. The paper identifies four escalating customer-AI risk states: Answer, Recommendation, Decision, and Commitment. Exposure increases when generated language moves from information into enterprise obligation. To govern this transition, the paper introduces the Machine Promise Control Architecture, structured around Authoritative Truth, Intent Classification, Authority Envelope, Verification Gate, Escalation and Redress, and Promise Telemetry. Three case studies demonstrate how machine output acquires authority in different operating environments. Cursor shows how generated language became perceived company policy. Rite Aid illustrates machine classification entering customer-facing operational action without adequate safeguards. McDonald’s and IBM demonstrate how conversational interpretation errors propagate into transaction errors, fulfilment problems, rework, and customer impact. Across all three cases, the common failure occurs when machine output acquires credibility, workflow access, decision rights, or customer reliance without corresponding control. The paper further separates AI authority into three distinct permissions: Say, Decide, and Execute. It introduces Promise Surface Area as an executive management model for assessing exposure based on interaction volume, promise-capable intents, authority scope, and consequence. It also applies Six Sigma disciplines through Critical-to-Quality measures, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, and the Cost of Poor Promise Quality, linking customer-AI governance directly to operating economics. The central proposition is that customer-facing AI should be governed as a complete decision system rather than as a conversational interface. Enterprises need explicit controls over what AI says, decides, and executes, alongside governed knowledge, deterministic verification, meaningful human escalation, decision lineage, promise-quality measurement, and structured incident recovery. The objective is controlled autonomy, with machine authority expanding only as quickly as the organisation’s ability to govern the resulting commitments.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 18 August 2026.
title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 32: When AI Makes the Wrong Promise to Your Customer

summary: Modern physics achieves extraordinary predictive precision, and it has been taught that the strange picture attached to its equations is what nature is: a wave that is a wave of nothing, a particle that is nowhere until observed, action at a distance with no carrier, fields with no medium. That picture was not discovered. It was adopted because the equations worked, and the equations themselves say nothing about it. This framework holds that the equations describe something physical, and sets out to say what: space is a physical medium with material properties, matter consists of structures within it, and the phenomena of the quantum, electromagnetic, relativistic and cosmological domains follow mechanically from that one premise. The quantum part has now been simulated: a definite particle moving through such a medium, guided by its own wave, produces the double-slit interference pattern (Atallah 2026). What this framework explains where current physics offers only the formalism: Quantum mechanics: Double-slit interference, entanglement correlations, measurement effects, and wave-particle duality emerge from compression waves in spatial medium interacting with definite particle structures. A particle's acceleration disturbs the medium; the disturbance disperses, and the part whose group velocity matches the particle's speed travels with it, with a wavelength set by the particle's momentum through the medium's dispersion—higher momentum, shorter wavelength. When approaching a barrier with slits, the bow wave reaches the slits first (several wavelengths ahead of the particle), diffracts through both openings, and creates an interference pattern before the particle arrives. The particle passes through one slit; beyond the slits its wave has fanned into lanes of constructive interference, and the particle, taking its direction from the wave's flow, follows a lane to the screen. Particles land on the bright bands. The interference pattern follows sinc-squared envelope (from rectangular slit geometry via Fourier transform) multiplied by cosine-squared fringes (from two-source interference)—pure wave mechanics in spatial medium. This single mechanism explains why slow electrons create wide patterns while fast electrons create narrow patterns, why red light diffracts differently than blue light, and why the relationship follows λ = h/p for all particles. No wave function collapse, no particles "being waves," no action at a distance, no ontological uncertainty—just definite particles creating momentum-dependent compression waves in a physical medium, with each particle independently steered by its own wave's interference pattern. This mechanism has been simulated in a particle medium with no constant fitted to the pattern: one disturbance at launch, a silent coast, and a single rule for direction reproduce the two-slit pattern of the wave itself, its scaling with wavelength, and its disappearance when one slit is closed (Atallah 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22701500). Electromagnetism: All phenomena from DC through optical frequencies emerge from two particle types in spatial medium. Teslons (field mediators with orientation and rotation degrees of freedom) create static electric and magnetic fields. Photons (propagating structures) carry current in conductors and electromagnetic energy in free space. This unified mechanism explains transmission lines, inductors, capacitors, the photoelectric effect, antennas, the right-hand rule, and the Meissner effect—all from spatial medium mechanics through photon-teslon-photon conversion processes. Cosmology: Hubble redshift, supernova time stretching, and CMB uniformity result from photon energy loss and propagation delays through spatial medium over cosmological distances. No Big Bang, no cosmic inflation, no dark energy required. Galaxy rotation curves result from extended compression fields around supermassive black holes, not invisible matter—explaining 40+
title: Universal Mechanics: A Unified Physics Framework

summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted mathematical discovery, program search, and formal reasoning motivate a practical design question: how can a long-horizon open problem be reorganized into a broad, falsifiable, and evidence-accountable human–AI search? We present a prospective candidate-engineering framework, grounded in a source-bound retrospective Phase-I design case on arithmetic dynamical structures relevant to the Hilbert–Pólya programme. The paper does not claim a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a completed Hilbert–Pólya realization, or a spectral identification of Riemann zeros. The framework has three layers. In Layer 1, a mathematician fixes a mathematical origin, permitted data, and an admissible transformation class; the present case uses a prime-symbolic origin, whereas a new mathematician-supplied basic idea begins a new Layer-1 record. In Layer 2, mathematician and AI jointly draft and version-freeze an AGENTS.md contract specifying candidate identity, lineage, gates, controls, portfolio policy, and stopping rules. In Layer 3, bounded AI work returns a source-linked evidence handoff for mathematician review. The accompanying roadmap requires a single candidate to establish an endogenous arithmetic source, orbit/repetition ownership, and a same-object zeta or determinant before stronger analytic and operator obligations are considered. The case comprises one early exploration entry and five system-family sessions. Its P1 Wiki retains catalogued provenance records rather than a common score of completed papers, theorems, or Route advances. No source-bound top-level direction documents an integrated same-object A0+A1+A2 chain in one natural candidate. We therefore motivate a broader but lineage-filtered candidate portfolio, screened early for arithmetic, clock, and determinant ownership rather than assembled retrospectively from partial successes. The associated Wiki is a provenance and navigation resource designed to preserve positive local results, controls, scoped failures, and reuse boundaries for subsequent researchers.
