summary: Circular economy is the trend that has emerged as an urgent necessity for manufacturing companies trying to break the linear "take, make, dispose" production cycle. While there is a significant amount of research happening in the circularity domain, the body of knowledge is split and does not necessarily connect with other theories, concepts and with application in different industrial sectors. The aim of this study was to develop an integrated conceptual framework to overcome the existing ambiguities in the field of CE and to facilitate further research while synthesizing the various streams of research on the topic. Methods: The articles were systematically identified from Web of Science and Scopus databases, and then snowballing was performed, in compliance with the PRISMA guidelines, between 2010 and 2025, and resulted in the identification of 100 articles. A tripartite analytical technique based on the use of quantitative bibliometric analysis, qualitative bibliographic content analysis and conceptual mapping was used. Results: The major thematic clusters that emerged were: circular supply chains, design for circularity, industrial symbiosis, Industry 4.0 enablers, policy and governance, performance measurement. The key practices of CE were identified and categorized according to the 4R and 10R frameworks, reverse logistics, industrial symbiosis and digital support for resource recovery at the micro, meso and macro level. The analysis shows that there are organizational, financial, technological and regulatory challenges that remain unaddressed, and that there is a significant lack of empirical evidence on a larger scale. Conclusions: There is a coherent conceptual framework linking CE principles with supply chain operations and Industry 4.0 technologies in this review and it proposes a prioritized future research direction that covers eight critical knowledge gaps. Government, industry and academia receive practical guidance on how to speed circular transitions in manufacturing.
tags: Circular economy, manufacturing, systematic literature review, supply chain management, Industry 4.0, PRISMA, reverse logistics, sustainability, resource recovery, 4R framework
title: Circular Economy in Manufacturing Industries: A Literature Review and Future Research Agenda

summary: Assistance can make a person's decision possible while leaving the person vulnerable to interpretive substitution and control of the available options. This paper develops a framework for adult disability support when will and preferences admit several warranted interpretations. Decision authorship is distinguished from causal responsiveness, functional performance, legal capacity, the validity of a particular act, and responsibility. A set-valued model separates semantic fidelity from authority over support and menus. Conditional results characterize compatible outcomes under interpretive uncertainty, changes under additional evidence, and the limited relation between menu expansion and compatibility. Counterexamples show that reversing every expressed preference satisfies sensitivity, that a constant outcome can satisfy fidelity, and that accurate selection within a restricted menu can coexist with an objectionable exclusion of alternatives. A temporal extension distinguishes learning about an earlier preference from forming a present preference through support. A finite branchwise result identifies when clarification permits compatible implementation despite an empty initial intersection. The normative discussion confronts CRPD Article 12, the Committee's corrected General Comment No. 1, selected provisions of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, and a prior proposal for interpretive support. A fictional community-participation decision demonstrates the audit, including disagreement, refusal, revision and supporter conflict. The resulting framework makes uncertainty and authority answerable without converting mathematical compatibility into permission to decide for another person. Empirical validation and case-specific legal application remain open.
title: Preserving Decision Authorship under Uncertain Interpretation of Will and Preferences in Adult Disability Support

summary: Overview  This repository contains the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, surrogate model training scripts, NSGA-II multi-objective optimization suite, and raw experimental outputs supporting the manuscript: "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity" Abstract Traditional concrete mix design usually involves lengthy empirical trial-and-error procedures. This study proposes a CatBoost–NSGA-II framework for multi-objective optimisation of concrete mixes, including leakage-controlled evaluation, uncertainty-aware strength feasibility, repeated-run robustness, and strength-floor sensitivity analysis. To evaluate the surrogate models, a source-study-grouped evaluation protocol consisting of ten repeated train–test splits was employed. The compressive strength model obtained only moderate performance (R^2 = 0.654 ± 0.062), whereas the RCPT model exhibited unstable performance (R^2 = -1.01 ± 3.07) and was therefore not included in the optimisation constraints. An uncertainty-aware lower confidence bound was used for strength feasibility, and the buildability constraints were incorporated into NSGA-II. For the 40 MPa case, 20 separate runs resulted in a robust 15-member Pareto front with an 86.7% recurrence rate. The mixture chosen had estimated reductions of 50.0% in embodied carbon and 22.7% in material cost as compared with a baseline that had the same strength. Nevertheless, the benefits decreased as the strength floor was raised and became statistically no different from zero at 70 MPa. Experimental verification based on physical tests is necessary before the approach can be applied in practice. Repository Structure  * 1_data/: Processed concrete mix dataset (processed_dataset_1867_records.csv) and RCPT sub-dataset (rcpt_subset_203.csv).  * 2_code/: Python codebase including data_cleaner.py, train_catboost.py, nsga2_optimization.py, and run_full_pipeline.py.  * models/: Serialized .joblib CatBoost surrogate model binaries and uncertainty parameters.  * results/: Raw Pareto front outputs across 20 independent seed runs (pareto_front_seed_42.csv through seed_61.csv) and consolidated multi-run front metrics.  * Root: reproducibility_manifest.yaml, data_dictionary.csv, exclusion_log.csv, and main entrypoint run_all.py. Instructions for Reproducibility  * Extract concrete_mix_zenoda.zip.  * Install requirements: pip install -r 2_code/requirements.txt.  * Execute python run_all.py to re-run data cleaning, surrogate training, and multi-objective optimization.
tags: CatBoost · NSGA-II · Concrete Mix Design · Multi-Objective Optimisation · Data Leakage · Embodied Carbon · Sensitivity Analysis
title: Data and Code Artifacts for "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity"

summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. Robustness checks include Newey–West HAC standard errors, alternative bandwidths, leave-one-out tests, influential-year exclusions, winsorization, placebo leads, and multiple-testing corrections using the Benjamini–Hochberg, Holm, and Bonferroni procedures. All data preparation and statistical analyses were conducted in R. The results show that Turkish and Greek naval procurement processes are temporally connected rather than independent. The strongest delivery-to-delivery association appears at a two-year lag. Greek naval deliveries are also associated with Turkish international naval orders one year later, while reverse-direction models identify associations between Turkish deliveries and subsequent Greek international orders. The overall pattern is consistent with reciprocal and temporally clustered modernization cycles rather than a fixed one-way action–reaction process. The repository includes cleaned analytical datasets, R scripts, figures, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, citation metadata, and the manuscript. Raw proprietary or redistribution-restricted source files are not included; users should consult the original SIPRI and World Bank sources where applicable. Version 1.2 adds the reviewer-requested stationarity diagnostics, first-difference sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-programme-window-out tests. The revised package also includes updated regression outputs and the reviewer-revised manuscript. The main research design and core delivery-to-delivery finding remain unchanged.
title: Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025: Replication Data and Code

summary: Environmental awareness involves understanding the fragility of the environment and the importance of its protection. As population growth, industrialization, and urbanization continue to intensify, natural resources are increasingly threatened, leading to environmental challenges such as pollution, climate change, global warming, acid rain, and ecosystem degradation. This study examined the correlates of students’ beliefs on environmental protection, focusing on awareness, compliance, and selected sociodemographic factors. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 938 students from the different colleges of Cagayan State University–Carig Campus, the largest campus in terms of student population. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Pearson product-moment correlation, and multiple linear regressions. Results revealed that students exhibited a high level of beliefs regarding environmental issues and concerns, with an overall weighted mean of 3.87. Among the dimensions assessed, environmental concern obtained the highest rating (x̄= 4.26), followed by environmental attitude (x̄= 4.09), green consumption (x̄= 3.95), and economic growth control (x̄= 3.84), while anthropocentric beliefs were rated at a moderate level (x̄= 3.21). Significant differences in environmental beliefs were observed across year level ( p = 0.003), nationalism ( p  < 0.001), religiosity ( p  < 0.001), expectation in life ( p = 0.001), and expectation in the future ( p = 0.041), but not across gender ( p = 0.235) and college affiliation ( p = 0.095). Furthermore, environmental awareness, compliance, nationalism, year level, awareness of environmental management laws, and level of satisfaction significantly predicted students’ beliefs regarding environmental protection. published by the Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Sciences | JBES
title: Correlates of students' beliefs on environmental protection: Awareness, compliance, and sociodemographic influences

summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.
title: BanglaVLP-5K: A Curated High-Resolution Image Dataset of Bangladeshi Vehicles and Licence Plates in Real-World Traffic Environments

This paper develops a first-passage model for architecture selection under finite-horizon failure risk. u)\,dt+\sqrt{v(b)}\,dW_t, \qquad Y_0=m, with failure at Y=0Y=0 . The resulting finite-horizon survival probability is available in closed form, allowing the optimal breadth b∗(m,ν;θ)=arg⁡max⁡0≤b≤1S(m,ν,b;θ)b^*(m,

The model supports specialist, mixed, and generalist survival optima. For linear breadth-dependent drift and variance, the derivative of survival with respect to breadth reduces to a compact stationarity condition involving the Gaussian inverse Mills ratio. An interior mixed architecture is possible only in a specific parameter regime, yielding an explicit timescale feasibility condition for mixed strategies. The paper also derives a drift-dependent variance result. Higher drift always improves finite-horizon survival, but lower variance is not universally beneficial. When the deterministic trajectory remains above the failure boundary over the horizon, variance strictly reduces survival. When deterministic drift would carry the system through the failure boundary, moderate variance can instead increase survival and produce a unique nonzero survival-maximizing variance. This defines a variance-rescue regime in which stochastic excursions can preserve systems that are deterministically doomed. The resulting framework does not assert that low margin or rapid environmental change universally favors generalism. Instead, margin and environmental timescale locate the system within a first-passage selection problem, while domain-specific drift, mismatch, and variance tradeoffs determine the preferred architecture. This version supersedes the earlier Margin–Variance Selector formulation, which treated the (m,ν)(m,
u) plane as carrying a generic architecture boundary without deriving that boundary from an absorbing-failure model. The present version replaces that claim with an exact first-passage selector and identifies the conditions under which specialist, mixed, generalist, and variance-rescue regimes occur.

summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. summary: An interface standard is advisory when nothing checks conformance to it, and normative when an external mechanism does. Python's public-interface convention is advisory: PEP 8 recommends that a library declare which symbols are contractual, but nothing enforces it, unlike Java, C++, or Rust. Every library therefore ships two surfaces at once — the declared surface it intends to support and the reachable surface clients can and do import — yet no prior work has measured how much of a library's surface is declared, how much of what clients consume is undeclared, or whether declaration predicts stability. We formalise a five-tier declaration ladder, computable statically from a distribution artifact, and measure it across 163 widely used libraries (81 AI/ML, 82 general-purpose controls) over up to 12 minor releases, together with a uniform sample of 30,000 PyPI projects yielding 14,213 client wheels and 12,704 clients contributing 419,752 import edges. The declared surface is tiny (only 7.4% of reachable symbols); clients over-select it by 5.9×, yet 56.5% (45.3% after a recall correction) of consumed edges remain undeclared, affecting 80.2% of client packages, though clients respect the underscore convention far more than __all__. Declaration status does predict removal — undeclared symbols disappear 1.5–2.5× as often as declared ones — and the AI/ML stack is not worse at signalling than general-purpose Python, only larger and faster-moving. The result is a repeatable, low-cost measurement that a standardisation process could run every release to check whether its own advisory recommendations are being followed.
tags: Python, advisory standards, standards conformance, public API, software evolution, empirical software engineering, machine learning.
title: replication package for Measuring Conformance to an Advisory Interface Standard: The Undeclared API Surface of the Python AI/ML Ecosystem

summary: Dark Forest arguments commonly reduce interstellar strategy to a bilateral encounter between two persistent civilisations. A galaxy, however, is an open population in which civilisations enter, disappear, form selective relationships and occupy a spatially constrained network. This paper develops a continuous-time Galactic Network Formation Game integrating demographic turnover, endogenous trust links, directed hostile reach, coalition formation, causal delay and extinction cascades. Civilisations arise at vacant sites and disappear through baseline, predatory and coordination hazards. Pairwise-stable trust links possess an exact distance threshold expressed with the Lambert W function. In a homogeneous three-dimensional field, the model derives a critical entry rate for formation of a giant trusted component. Coalition governance is constrained by a causal-diameter bound, which can make several galactic cliques necessary even when a topological giant component exists. A congestion-security payoff yields conditions for a unique locally stable coalition size. Coalition survival under random or targeted extinction is represented by core pruning, with closed mean-field equations for cascade size. Numerical illustrations reveal sparse archipelagos, brittle cliques, resilient cliques and temporally admissible federations. Cosmic silence, cooperation and pre-emption are therefore network-level outcomes rather than universal consequences of uncertainty.
title: From Two Players to a Galactic Network: Entry, Extinction, Coalitions, Cliques and Spatial Topology in Interstellar Strategic Interaction

summary: Reproducibility package supporting an analysis of sustainability transition in Sarawak, Malaysia. The repository contains curated analytical and processed datasets, acquisition and processing notebooks, model outputs, robustness analyses, figures, quality-assurance records, provenance documentation and detailed reproduction guidance. The research examines whether low-carbon development constitutes a sustainability transition when ecological integrity, biodiversity and climate-conditioned environmental vulnerability are considered alongside energy and development outcomes. The package contains 103 scientific files together with repository control documentation. Eleven public-facing scientific files were prepared as portability-safe or publication-safe copies without changing the underlying scientific results. Three RQ5 outputs carry explicit provenance warnings because their original computational specification could not be fully reconstructed; these limitations are transparently documented. Third-party and derived datasets remain governed by their original licensing and attribution terms.
title: Sarawak Sustainability Transition Reproducibility Package

summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.
title: Deriving the Pure Price of Anarchy for Networked Resource Allocation Games

summary: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. Existing agentic memory systems address this limitation but generally operate at the individual-user level, restricting the public knowledge that could be shared across users to improve downstream responses. We introduce AIM (Agentic Interoperable Memory), a unified, privacy-aware memory framework that enables multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems to persistently manage private and shared memory. AIM dynamically classifies information as private, scoped to one user and inaccessible to others, or public, accessible to all users. It enforces index-level access controls so that private memories are retrievable only by their owner, protecting sensitive data while allowing beneficial shared knowledge to improve coordination and consistency. We also introduce MUMBench (Multi-User Memory Benchmark), a dataset of multi-user interactions containing private and shareable information across four domains. To our knowledge, MUMBench is the first public dataset designed to evaluate multiple memory operations, including retrieval, creation, update, and deletion, in a multi-user environment. Across three independent runs on MUMBench, AIM achieves 96.0% visibility classification accuracy, 58.8% strict operation accuracy, and 70.5% state-aware operation accuracy.
title: AIM: A Privacy-Aware Interoperable Memory Framework for Multi-Agent Multi-User LLM Systems

summary: Periodic multilayer mirrors for X-rays require a layer period held to about 0.02 nm, set by deposition rates held in the laboratory's own notebook. A large language model agent was given a target multilayer specification and read access to a laboratory archive. Deposition recipes were authored in the native recipe language of a magnetron sputtering system and submitted through a Model Context Protocol bridge of 17 tools in three tiers, with enforcement held in the control application. The target was a 30-bilayer Ru/C multilayer with a period of 6.85 nm, a pair chosen because each period is fitted as two layers. The agent could write only inside a working project of its own, so it could alter neither the calibration it read nor the measurements that scored it. Mirrors were scored against a human-authored reference by X-ray reflectivity, and the 3% acceptance threshold on relative period difference was fixed before deposition. Across four scored agent-authored depositions the relative period difference fell from 20% on the calibration as given to 2.26% after one measured-feedback iteration and 0.79% after a second. Sixteen failure modes of the agent-facing interface were identified. The result is bounded to the period, pair and chamber observed.
title: Agent-authored deposition recipes for X-ray multilayer mirrors: schema-bound LLM control of a magnetron sputtering system with reflectivity-verified outcomes

summary: The paper studies finite-horizon ruin for an insurance company with several lines of business admitting heavy-tailed claims. The claim amount process of the insurance company is modeled as a multivariate increasing Lévy process possibly perturbed with fluctuations. A relevant insolvency event may involve the failure of a single line, of several lines at once, or of groups of lines linked through internal transfers, reinsurance, or a guarantee arrangement. These events have different geometries and need not occur on the same probability scale. Under asymptotic tail independence among claims from different lines, classical regular variation assigns zero limiting probability to a multi-line failure and is therefore unable to identify either the ruin probability or the corresponding solvency capital requirement. Using a multivariate Lévy process to model cumulative claims and regular variation on a nested sequence of subcones of the positive orthant to model dependence across lines, we provide the exact scaling rate of the ruin probability and the limit behavior. Additionally, explicit computations are presented for examples with independent business lines, common arrivals of independent claims, Gaussian copula dependent claims, Marshall-Olkin dependent claims, and bipartite insurance networks. Finally, we use Monte Carlo simulations to support our theoretical findings.
title: Multivariate Ruin in Lévy-driven Insurance Risk Models under Heavy Tails

summary: Question-answering often requires reasoning across multiple connected facts rather than retrieving a single isolated relation. Knowledge graphs (KGs) provide a structured way to represent such facts, but training large language models (LLMs) only on isolated KG head-relation-tail triples may limit their ability to learn the surrounding context needed for multi-hop reasoning. In this work, we propose a context-augmented training framework for multi-hop question-answering. Although generally applicable, we validate the framework in the context of disease-specific KGs, extracted using a reliable KG extraction framework called GraphMERT, for Gastroparesis and Diabetes. For each primary KG triple, we attach supporting triples extracted from the same source text chunk to form a context graph (CG). This creates two supervision settings: KG-grounded supervision, which uses only the target KG triple or path, and CG-grounded supervision, which uses the target KG triple or path together with supporting context triples. We train the Qwen3-14B model using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) under both settings, producing KGModel and CGModel variants. To strengthen the lower-hop factual foundation of the models, we introduce an LLM-judged, history-aware adaptive repair pipeline that identifies unresolved one-hop failures, continually fine-tunes on targeted repair examples, and removes or quarantines problematic noisy triples. This repair stage enables the models to reach 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets. Finally, we employ reinforcement learning (RL) using lower-hop question-answer items and evaluate generalization on harder 3-hop, 4-hop, and 5-hop tasks. Across both diseases, context-augmented supervision consistently improves multi-hop performance over KG-only supervision. RL initialized from repaired SFT checkpoints yields larger and more stable gains.
title: Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering

summary: Prompt-policy editing offers a practical way to improve agents that synthesize executable workflows without updating the underlying model. However, persistent prompt editing has two coupled properties. First, edit locality does not imply effect locality: an edit confined to one policy segment can ripple through downstream execution, altering behavior beyond the edited segment. Second, edit effects are composition-sensitive: edits that work in isolation can interfere after composition, causing one or both to lose their benefit or become harmful. Persistent adaptation must therefore support two distinct decisions: identifying where the policy should change from execution feedback, and determining whether the resulting edit remains safe to persist after composition. To address these challenges, we introduce RIPPLE (Replay-Informed Persistent Policy Localization and Editing), which separates where an edit is made from whether it remains safe after composition. It diagnoses failed trajectories, maps each actionable failure to a predefined policy segment, and restricts the correction to that part of the policy. RIPPLE then evaluates candidates against the same iteration-start policy to compare their isolated gains, before replaying promising edits after previously accepted updates to expose downstream effects and interactions. Only edits that remain safe under composition are retained. We evaluate RIPPLE on Flow-HO, a synthetic held-out benchmark for executable workflow synthesis. RIPPLE improves validation success by up to 23.1% and yields positive gains on two additional frozen language-model backbones, while maintaining edit efficiency and low execution cost. Targeted interaction analysis further demonstrates both properties: a segment-local tool-use edit changes downstream resource resolution and validation, while an edit beneficial in isolation becomes harmful after composition.
title: Local Edits, Global Ripples: Replay-Informed Policy Adaptation for Workflow Synthesis

summary: Agent evaluations can be numerically correct while measuring a different construct from the one implied by their labels. We present a retrospective measurement audit of selected Praxa AI implementation files, historical evaluation artifacts, and operational records. A 139-case offline routing report contains 112 passes and 27 failures despite zero gating failures, because known gaps are explicitly exempted from the gate. An identifier-free export represents 8,843 tool-attempt rows: 8,395 recorded durations and 448 missing values. Of the durations, 121 equal the signed 32-bit maximum and carry abandoned-client labels; inspected database code clamps elapsed lifecycle age. The pooled recorded 99th percentile is 2,147,483,647 ms, versus 38,118.31 ms among server-observed completed calls. This is a stratum contrast, not a treatment effect. In a documented single-trajectory compaction pilot, the reported follow-up input reduction is 94.39%, but the reduction across the trigger and follow-up calls together is 46.54%. We reproduce the descriptive calculations, verify 91 timing statistics through a separate weighted rational-arithmetic implementation, and execute 13 scoring-function and 12 analysis-verifier tests. Finite-completion bounds show how missing durations limit all-row timing statements without imputing values. The contribution is a source-linked case study and reusable verification package for separating gate policy, lifecycle timing, and request-level accounting from broader agent-performance claims. Historical provider runs and the full current pipeline were not independently reproduced; general capability superiority and population-level statistical significance are not established.
title: When Agent Metrics Measure Different Things: An Evidence-Grounded Audit of the Praxa AI Pipeline

summary: From Wave Confinement to Recursive AI Instability: A Propagation-Correction Criticality Law and Successful Prospective Prediction Richard J. Reyes - September 14, 2026 YouTube:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q7Tr7GXvfMI This paper develops a mathematical bridge from Wave Confinement Theory (WCT) stability dynamics to recursive artificial-intelligence instability through a propagation-correction criticality law. Starting from the WCT Lyapunov framework, it derives a local rate-based description in which destabilizing propagation competes with restoring correction and identifies a dimensionless criticality ratio governing whether perturbations decay, remain marginal, or grow. The resulting framework is then applied to a previously frozen WCT/RCA prediction. A prospective stabilization ratio of approximately R_pred = 0.0100, specified before the later 2026 multi-agent incident analyzed here, is compared with an independently reconstructed event value of approximately R_2026 = 0.0104. The two values differ by approximately 4%.
