title: Photographic documentation for the safeguarding of the cultural landscape of Sternatia: a system of interrelated records within the conceptual and documentary framework of conservation-restoration. Project "Il comune griko di Sternatia tra patrimoni e tradizioni culturali. Il ruolo della digitalizzazione per la valorizzazione del territorio". Salento University (Italy), Department of Legal Sciences.

summary: Large language models (LLMs) process long contexts, including long documents and lengthy conversations, but face token-level memory usage that increases proportionally to input length. Although model optimization and lossy prompt compression are widely used, these methods still fail to solve the long-context recall problem beyond pretrained and size-constrained context windows. This paper proposes a long-context recall method that maintains near-constant GPU memory usage as context length increases, without additional training. The main idea is to reconstruct facts using parameter activations in the LLM's feed-forward layers, which store residual vectors representing facts from the source document. Utilizing residual vectors allows the LLM to deterministically reconstruct query relevant facts without referencing the original document, preserving high fidelity and reducing memory usage without fine-tuning weights. Experimental results show that the proposed method enables answering single-fact questions in two-million-token story contexts where previous methods fail.
title: Residual Vector-based Reconstruction as Long-Context Recall Regardless of Context Window Size

summary: Generative recommendation (GR) relies on large-beam decoding to generate hundreds of candidate items, creating a new scaling challenge for recurrent linear attention. Existing linear attention serving systems either materialize a full recurrent state for every beam or repeatedly replay shared history, incurring substantial memory and traffic overhead. To address this, we present OneLA, a linear-attention decoding framework that exploits the shared prompt and short divergent suffixes of GR workloads. Specifically, OneLA represents all beam states using a single shared prompt-derived state and compact, append-only records of their divergent transitions. Using this representation, OneLA computes only the state information required at each decoding step, without reconstructing a full recurrent state for every beam. Furthermore, OneLA uses a lightweight ancestry index to track the transition records that make up each beam's history, allowing beams to be updated without moving or copying existing records. A fused GPU kernel further reuses the shared state across beams. Our analysis shows that OneLA achieves 1.54-2.46x end-to-end decode speedups while substantially reducing recurrent-state memory use and data movement.
title: OneLA: Scaling Linear-Attention Decoding to Large Beams in Generative Recommendation

summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

summary: Hierarchical correlations are a universal feature of any realistic model of data, and the question of how associative memory models may learn these correlations and generalize beyond them to construct new sensible images is an important step towards understanding more complex modern architectures such as diffusion models. We consider a hierarchical model for memories which are sampled and stored in a dense Hopfield network with polynomial activation. We analytically derive conditions for each level of this hierarchy to be locally stable - that is they are local energy minima. We use prototype reconstruction as a minimal model of generalization and we find that it takes only a quasi-polynomial amount of information to generalize beyond particular memories and even particular groups in the hierarchy. We observe a qualitatively analogous phase diagram in the number of memories, sharpness of the activation function (polynomial degree) for data from Fashion-MNIST.
title: Hierarchical Prototype Emergence in Modern Hopfield Models

summary: Parametric models of the human head are essential tools traditionally used in computer vision and graphics for animation, rendering, and reconstruction. More recently, they serve as crucial conditioning signals within generative large vision models, allowing for tight spatial control of generated imagery. However, existing publicly available models are typically limited in anatomical scope, modeling only outer geometry while ignoring intra-oral and ocular structures, and frequently suffer from reduced geometric quality stemming from low-fidelity input datasets. In this report we introduce a new parametric model dubbed Generative aNthropometric Model (GNM), named as a homophone of the human genome. GNM encompasses the head, face, neck, eyeballs, teeth, and tongue, and it is built on an extensive database of high-resolution 3D scans combined with high-quality anatomy specific artist-made samples. This report details the data provenance, the model architecture including the specialized sub-models for the ocular and intra-oral structures, and shows its SotA performance on fitting target 3D face scans. To foster community innovation, the complete GNM framework is made publicly available.
title: GNM Head: A Generative aNthropometric Model of the human head

summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) creates a structural advantage for offloading: only a small fraction of activated experts need to reside in device memory, and if they can be loaded in time for computation, offloading can in principle approach full-load performance, where all model weights reside in device memory. Yet translating MoE's structural advantage into practical offloading gains remains challenging. We propose SeqMoE to bridge this gap. To maximize expert hits, we build predictive memory management: (i) Sequence-to-sequence prediction. We are the first to recast expert activation prediction as sequence modeling, enabling accurate multi-step, multi-layer forecasts that provide a long and reliable window for downstream decisions. (ii) Joint prefetch scheduling. We formulate prefetch scheduling as Job Sequencing with Deadlines to maximize expected expert hits and improve bandwidth efficiency. (iii) Forecast-driven caching. Leveraging the recursive nature of sequence modeling, we introduce a probabilistic Belady policy for future-aware eviction. To eliminate execution bottleneck, we develop (iv) Graph-compatible offloading runtime. We derive general runtime principles encompassing compute-transparent expert placement and synchronization-free orchestration disciplines for end-to-end graph capture. With 45% expert residency, SeqMoE averages a 96.97% hit rate and 80.22% of full-load performance, advancing the state of the art in MoE offloading.
title: SeqMoE: Toward Full-Load Performance via Predictive and Graph-Compatible MoE Offloading

summary: The proliferation of highly capable open-weight Small Language Models (SLMs) democratizes access to advanced cybersecurity capabilities, posing a escalating risk as these models can bypass proprietary API guardrails when deployed locally. However, SLMs deployed as autonomous agents often struggle with long-horizon, exploratory tasks like cybersecurity Capture The Flag (CTF) challenges due to context bloat and cognitive degradation from accumulated tool-call outputs. To understand and mitigate this cybersecurity threat, we introduce \textit{context segmentation}, a two-level agentic framework that divides complex exploitation tasks into manageable, contextually isolated sub-problems. Evaluating on the \texttt{picoCTF} dataset using memory-constrained \texttt{gemma-4} models, we demonstrate that for the E4B model, our strategy acts as an intelligent search, achieving competitive rewards with superior token efficiency compared to brute-force retries, and successfully solving 18.52\% of tasks that standard agentic execution fails to complete. Code is available at https://github.com/9xeb/context-segmentation.
title: Evaluating Context Segmentation in Locally Deployable SLMs for Cybersecurity CTF Tasks

summary: sEMG is vulnerable to various contaminants that distort signal morphology and spectral content. Accurate signal quality assessment (SQA) is essential for identifying such degradation and ensuring reliable clinical analyses and decisions. Recent neural network-based SQA methods achieve accurate quality estimation by learning complex contamination patterns, yet their black-box nature prevents clinicians from understanding or validating the reported scores and limits adaptability to application-specific quality definitions without retraining. To address these limitations, we propose Prism-SQA, an interpretable and adaptable neural framework that reformulates SQA as a physiology-aware source-separation and verification process. Prism-SQA decomposes each input signal into a clean sEMG component and five contaminant-specific components using a U-Net with bidirectional long short-term memory. Each separated contaminant component is examined by a Contaminant Fingerprint Verifier, which enforces physiological plausibility by comparing its temporal and spectral structure with canonical contaminant signatures. This design allows clinicians to inspect how each contaminant affects signal quality, grounding the assessment in transparent, signal-level evidence rather than opaque latent representations. Quality indices computed from the verified components further enable customization of quality criteria across clinical contexts without retraining. We evaluate Prism-SQA on continuous quality-score estimation using synthesized noisy sEMG from public Ninapro datasets and on binary quality classification using a clinical dysphagia dataset. Results show that Prism-SQA achieves competitive or better performance than contemporary black-box neural methods while providing explicit interpretability and adaptability, advancing toward practical and clinically aligned sEMG SQA.
title: Prism-SQA: An Interpretable and Adaptable Neural Framework for Surface Electromyography Quality Assessment

summary: AI is beginning to make substantive contributions to LLM inference optimization. Existing AI optimizations are predominantly profiling-based. Profiling-bound feedback confines the search to the capabilities and performance of an existing software stack, preventing a fundamentally better architecture of LLM inference systems from being identified. To enable the AI-driven LLM inference system architecting loop, we argue that a general workload representation, a verifiable mutation space, and an implementation-independent evaluator are required. We present the RoofLang domain-specific language (DSL) that provides these features. In our evaluation, RoofLang reveals that DeepSeek V4-series models could achieve 3.5-39.5$\times$ higher peak decode throughput than other representative models. This gap is disproportionate to their total parameter counts and arises largely from compact KV-cache designs that support larger batches and reduce memory traffic. A persistent optimizer agent further discovered several new architectures that improved both throughput and interactivity of DeepSeek V4 Pro on NVIDIA B300 by 6.23-50.1%.
title: RoofLang: Enabling AI-Driven Architecting of LLM Inference Systems

summary: The book series The Stream and the Algebra presents a speculative research programme — a thought-experiment in the mathematics of relation, offered for scrutiny, not yet peer-reviewed or tested. Its wager: nothing physical is an absolute number (a mass means nothing until a unit is chosen), only how one quantity stands to another. It fixes the dimensionless relations the world determines and concedes one scale, the anchor; a firewall shares a structure's form across domains, never a bare number. Its sharpest stakes: an axion-free zero of strong CP, few-GeV asymmetric dark matter, and the tau mass from Koide read forward. From the fundamental particles it carries this idea to the vacuum, the classical world, and physics' open problems. Book VII asks where the flavour geometry comes from. It fixes one concrete, frozen heterotic string vacuum — a Z_6-II orbifold of the E_8×E_8 mini-landscape, its provenance settled before any measured number is consulted — and asks whether the single amplitude the Koide relation leaves free descends from it. The programme holds throughout to one firewall: a structure's form may cross domains, a bare number never; and it keeps the line between what the mathematics closes and what stays open. No physical grade is raised; the Koide value stays open. Book VII is issued at one frozen epoch as three parts under a single manifest and version stamp — Part VII.1 (Corpus & Conditional Layers), Part VII.2 (the monograph edition) and Part VII.3 (the internal Annexes: the Ω-sections and the revision history). Part VII.3, The Source and the Cube: The Annexes, is the append-only provenance record behind Book VII — the hundreds of dated Ω-findings, the routes tried and refuted, the corrections booked with banners, and the full revision chronicle. It is not a publication of record and is never the sole terminal support of a claim typed closed: it is the working behind Parts VII.1 and VII.2, hash-frozen and available on request. Its discipline is the firewall in action. Every finding carries a typed Grade block with B_3=0 throughout — no physical grade raised anywhere — and superseded claims are retained with inline supersession banners rather than deleted. The record documents the successive self- corrections that led to the current readings: the group-identity restoration to SmallGroup(648,597); the Koide rank correction, in which the earlier rank-2 reading K=2/3 at Kähler ratio ≈ 14 was recognised as the rank-two crossing (2+sqrt(3))^2 artefact and resolved in the source's favour to a genuine rank-3 three-mass landing; the mirror factorisation g(1+i)=2^1/4e^-iπ/24; and the strong-CP finite-representation phase (Φ_3=π present for the minimal Standard-Model colour sector — the modular symmetry does not by itself protect strong CP). It also carries the cross-pollination glosses toward the closed Books I–VI: the sqrt(2) read as a level-2 modular reflection value refining Book I's Pythagorean reading; the Fricke mirror confirming Book V's duality, not symmetry; and the rank-3 typing sharpening the conditional Koide of Books II and IV. These are reported here and never edit the closed volumes. Alongside the findings log the volume carries the remaining Layer-III apparatus: a reading guide and insertion register; Annex M on information, order and time and the purely- mathematical closure meta-structure; Annex, the numberless / form-computational apparatus with the closure-debt poset, the no-rescue and no-silent-conversion firewalls and the frontier passport; Appendix E, the R1 Execution and Replication Package specified for a stranger, with the run executed and verifier-accepted; and Appendix R, the revision history. summary: Presentation slides for “Can AI Read Coptic Ostraca? Formula, Fragment, and the Reconstruction of Meaning in O.Frangé 1–27,” presented at the online mini-conference AI for Ancient Studies (AI4AS), held as part of DH2026 (27–31 July 2026, Daejeon, South Korea). This study examines how three large language models, GPT-5.5 (accessed through ChatGPT), Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 5, translate Coptic documentary texts. The experiments were conducted through the services’ free-tier interfaces in July 2026, without task-specific fine-tuning or supplementary contextual information supplied by the researcher. Drawing on O.Frangé 1–27, a set of Coptic monastic letters from late antique Western Thebes, the presentation focuses on nine selected documents. AI-generated translations are compared with the published French translations, with particular attention to practical requests, epistolary formulas, fragmentary passages, and scriptural or religious language. Recurring translation errors and interpretive choices are analyzed as evidence of how LLMs reconstruct meaning. The analysis highlights four tendencies: completion bias, which turns incomplete passages into coherent statements; semantic inflation, which adds emotional or interpretive weight to conventional expressions; genre distortion, which recasts documentary communications as personal or devotional reflections; and the erasure of formulaic structure, which obscures repetition and epistolary conventions. The presentation argues that evaluating LLM translation in papyrology requires attention not only to linguistic accuracy but also to interpretive behavior, especially the handling of textual gaps, uncertainty, and documentary conventions.
title: Can AI Read Coptic Ostraca?: Formula, Fragment, and the Reconstruction of Meaning in O.Frangé 1–27

summary: Complete offline reproducibility package supporting the manuscript “Longitudinal particulate changes and temporally varying rainfall associations in a tropical river–wetland system”. This record contains a single self-contained ZIP archive with the fixed source inputs, 96 selected Sentinel-2 acquisitions, analysis scripts, calculated tables, figure-generation code, expected outputs, software distributions, dependency locks and SHA256 integrity manifests used for the study of particulate transfer in the Mandromondromotra river–wetland system, south-eastern Madagascar. The package provides a common offline entry point that reconstructs basin rainfall before propagating the regenerated rainfall series through the Sentinel analysis and rebuilding the retained analytical outputs, publication tables, figures and bilingual supplementary material. The workflow covers the historical gravimetric reconstruction, the 2015–2020 longitudinal TSS record, the 2022–2025 conductivity–turbidity mixing analysis, rainfall sensitivities, Sentinel-2 surface-state calculations and the associated reproducibility checks. The final archived package was validated through two independent cold executions from fresh extractions on Windows 11 x86_64 using the bundled software environment. Both complete runs returned exit code 0. The final validation reproduced 69/69 water-analysis outputs and 60/60 Sentinel outputs and generated the complete set of 20 publication assets. The archive contains 641 integrity-controlled fixed files. Archive file: Mandromondromotra_reproducibility_package_v1.0.zip Version: 1.0 SHA256: 3F4EAC0E541FD6937B9333D51A7795218018F0809CF0C99148F9A61A909273F8 The archive is intended to preserve the exact computational state used for reproducibility rather than to provide a continuously updated software repository. Bundled execution environments are provided for the supported target platforms; the final release documented here was cold-tested on Windows x86_64. This Zenodo record contains the reproducibility package only. The manuscript itself is not included in this deposit.
title: Reproducibility package for "Longitudinal particulate changes and temporally varying rainfall associations in a tropical river–wetland system"

summary: Replication materials for Alexeev & Weatherburn (2026), “When Punishment Changes the Rules: Sentencing, Licence Loss, and Measured Recidivism.” The paper studies how a sentence can change the legal rules that govern a person's subsequent conduct, and therefore what counts as measured recidivism. After a proven low-range drink-driving (PCA) offence in New South Wales, a Local Court magistrate chooses among three sentencing packages: (1) unconditional dismissal, (2) conditional nonconviction, and (3) a conviction-recording sentence, which almost always carries licence disqualification. The two nonconviction dispositions are instrumented jointly, using each magistrate's own sentencing propensity for each disposition, computed from cases outside the defendant's own court-time assignment block. A substantial share of the estimated reduction in subsequent proven offending following nonconviction falls in the offence of driving while disqualified or suspended — an offence whose legal possibility is itself created by the conviction-recording package. Recorded recidivism therefore combines behavioural responses with legal exposure created by punishment itself, and the paper argues that policy evaluation should measure the two separately. This deposit contains the analysis code, an independent reconstruction of the empirical pipeline, the presentation/validation code, all non-disclosive aggregate outputs and typeset tables the manuscript reports, the manuscript source and figures, and build/validation logs. It contains no unit-record data. The underlying NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research (BOCSAR) Reoffending Database extract is confidential administrative data supplied under a restricted-access agreement and cannot be redistributed by the authors. Researchers wishing to replicate or extend the analysis must apply directly to BOCSAR for access to a comparable extract ( https://bocsar.nsw.gov.au ). One magistrate-level aggregate export is additionally withheld pending explicit data-custodian clearance; see the included Data Availability Statement and README for details. This version (0.99) supersedes the version 1 (0.9) deposit under this same record, which corresponded to an earlier, withdrawn binary-treatment design under a different working title and does not reproduce the current paper. See README.md and Manuscript/revision_log.md in this deposit for the full version history.
title: Replication materials for "When Punishment Changes the Rules: Sentencing, Licence Loss, and Measured Recidivism"

summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.5321. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial tame knot type is at least 6.5321. This improves the 6.32 bound in version 1.0 by 0.2121. The proof combines essential-secant profiles, radial variational inequalities, ordered failure boundaries, and retained distortion constraints. The new comparison couples an actual last radial crossing on the initial arc with the same actual complementary split point, retaining both cyclic routes and common angular data. Necessary closed systems are excluded using directed interval arithmetic. Complete runs at 96-bit and 192-bit precision each certified all 54 original closed regions, testing 1,814,262 outer boxes per precision with no unresolved frontier. Independent mathematical, numerical and process-origin reviews passed. Fresh-extraction checks of the finished archive reproduced all 37 finite checks, the two-precision conditional component, and both full-receipt auditors. These checks supplement the complete original numerical runs. Version 2.0 contains the 19-page preprint and the complete reproducible LaTeX source and verification package, including frozen sources, full receipts, mathematical supplements, audit records and reproduction instructions. The package also documents structural research findings, unsuccessful approaches and remaining obstacles. No stronger global bound, knot upper bound, optimality, or proof-assistant formalization is claimed. The preprint has not been submitted to or accepted by a journal.
title: An improved lower bound for the distortion of a knotted curve

summary: This release adds openff_no_water-3.0.0-alpha2b.offxml and openff_no_water_unconstrained-3.0.0-alpha2b.offxml . We're releasing another alpha version of the OpenFF-3.0.0 "Rosemary" SMIRNOFF protein-and-small-molecule force field. In initial benchmarks, alpha2b appears to be at least comparable to alpha0 for proteins (if not better), and fixes several regressions in small molecule performance, achieving similar QM energy+geometry benchmark performance to the Sage force field line. We are not providing assets/scripts with this release since it's an alpha, but we will do so for the full 3.0.0 release. The best single source of information about alpha2b's performance is likely the slides and recording from the meeting where the alpha2b force field was benchmarked. We anticipate that the full openff-3.0.0 release will have the same structure as this alpha protein FF, in terms of using AshGC/NAGL charges (not library charges) and the approximate number and composition of SMIRKS parameters. This force field is a research tool and does not contain a water model, and probably has other pointy edges. It's likely you'll get the best results using OPC3 as the water model. If you do not use this in conjunction with a force field file containing a water model, the FF will still work, but your waters will be assigned hydroxyl parameters, will lack angle constraints, and will be very unphysical.
title: openforcefield/openff-forcefields

summary: ECLIPSE (Electroweak Capture and LZ Inelastic Phenomenology for Solar Exclusion) is a numerical framework for the combined study of direct detection, solar capture, and solar-neutrino constraints on pseudo-Dirac electroweak dark matter. The code accompanies the analysis of a Peccei–Quinn completion of a pseudo-Dirac electroweak doublet motivated by the 2026 LUX-ZEPLIN high-recoil search. It combines the terrestrial and solar calculations in a single reproducible Python pipeline. ECLIPSE computes the standard-thermal LZ Nsig=1N_{\rm sig}=1 branch, isotope-resolved finite-momentum xenon responses, accepted true nuclear-recoil spectra, inelastic dark-matter capture in the Sun, capture–annihilation evolution and post-capture diagnostics, and the corresponding comparison with IceCube solar-neutrino limits. The v0.5.4 release provides the public baseline used for the associated analysis. It includes read-only xenon-response caches that permit reproduction of the LZ recoil-spectrum diagnostics without a local dmscatter installation, together with checked reference outputs, numerical inputs, regression tests, and reproducibility documentation. The full solar-capture calculation can interface with dmscatter and WIMpy_NREFT for finite-momentum nuclear responses. ECLIPSE is intended to reproduce the calculations of the associated scientific analysis and is not a detector-level LUX-ZEPLIN likelihood. Version 0.5.4 passes 47 physics, regression, compatibility, and release-hygiene tests.
title: ECLIPSE: Electroweak Capture and LZ Inelastic Phenomenology for Solar Exclusion

summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly capable of performing research workflows that extend from idea generation and literature search to experimentation, analysis, manuscript production, and review. This development makes a previously backgrounded epistemic question newly visible: before an inquiry can be answered, how does a question come to arise at all? This commentary distinguishes the yuanqi (缘起) of a question—its historically situated emergence through relations, conditions, encounters, contingencies, and forms of lived concern—from both the subsequent process of inquiry and its terminal artifact. Human questions often emerge within particular histories, places, relationships, encounters, affects, contingencies, and forms of lived concern. Dialogical and narrative forms in philosophy and religious traditions can preserve such conditions rather than merely decorate detachable propositions. Journalism likewise depends not only on what is eventually reported, but on where inquiry begins, who encounters whom, which relation makes a phenomenon salient, and how an initial interpretation develops. Autonomous AI research does not invalidate these structures; rather, it makes their comparison urgent. The relevant distinction is not a metaphysical opposition between "existential" humans and "mechanical" machines, but the genealogy through which a question becomes worth asking for a given epistemic agent or system. The commentary argues that, as answers and even research questions become increasingly automatable, knowledge institutions should attend more carefully to the spatiotemporal, relational, contingent, and existential provenance of inquiry, and to forms of record capable of preserving the conditions under which later understanding can be regenerated.
title: Autonomous AI Research Makes the "Yuanqi (缘起) of Questions" a Genuine Question of Our Time

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly shaped education, with ChatGPT developed by OpenAI, emerging as a prominent tool due to its ability to generate contextually relevant language and support learning. This survey investigates the integration of ChatGPT into mathematics education, focusing on three dimensions. First, it explores innovative strategies for creating interactive and personalized learning environments that adapt to individual student needs. Second, it evaluates ChatGPT’s specific advantages in mathematics instruction, including providing tailored feedback, assisting with problem-solving, and deepening conceptual understanding. Third, it addresses the challenges of adopting ChatGPT in advanced mathematics education, such as risks of over-reliance, the necessity of balancing AI with traditional pedagogy, and the importance of ongoing professional development for educators. Recent studies highlight ChatGPT’s potential to solve complex mathematical problems, such as those in linear algebra and word problems, while also noting limitations related to accuracy and the preservation of critical thinking skills. The findings demonstrate that ChatGPT can significantly enhance mathematics education by supporting personalized learning and complex problem-solving. Therefore, this study will contribute to the discourse on AI in education by identifying opportunities, challenges, and implications for equity, pedagogy, and the responsible integration of ChatGPT in future classrooms.
title: A survey on leveraging artificial intelligence tools for enhancing advanced mathematical education and problem-solving

summary: Code for the Paper "More Efficient Secret-Shared Joins with Multiplicity via Oblivious Sort Expansion" This repository contains the official implementation of the paper "More Efficient Secret-Shared Joins with Multiplicity via Oblivious Sort Expansion." Join-OM : Implements the Join-OM protocol from AHK+ ( Secure Statistical Analysis on Multiple Datasets: Join and Group-By ) and our Join-OM protocol based on OSE. Includes checks to verify identical outputs. Join-MM : Our main Join-MM protocol with working examples. Join-MM-32 : Parameterized version (32-bit inputs, adjustable input size) for benchmarks against BDG+ ( Secret-Shared Joins with Multiplicity from Aggregation Trees ). Includes correctness verification. Join-MM-64 : Parameterized version (64-bit inputs, adjustable input size) for benchmarks against Scape ( Scape: Scalable Collaborative Analytics System on Private Database with Malicious Security ). Join-MM-AggTree-32 : Implementation of the BDG+ Join-MM protocol, using 32-bit inputs. 2. Scape Baseline Located in Join-OSE/scql/engine/operator/secret_join.cc . Note on Modification : We have modified the secret_join.cc and secret_join_test.cc files to support runtime profiling and performance testing of Scape. Pull and run the SPU Docker image: docker pull secretflow/ubuntu-base-ci:latest docker run -d -it --name spu-dev- $(whoami) \       --mount type = bind ,source = " $(pwd) " ,target = /home/admin/dev/ \       -w /home/admin/dev \       --cap-add = SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp = unconfined \       --cap-add = NET_ADMIN \       --privileged = true \     secretflow/ubuntu-base-ci:latest \       bash docker exec -it spu-dev- $(whoami) bash Mount/Place the code: Copy this entire repository into the container. WAN Emulation Run the following commands inside the container to emulate a WAN with 20 ms latency and 1 Gbit/s bandwidth: sudo tc qdisc del dev lo root 2 >/dev/null || true sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 20ms rate 1gbit limit 10000 export SPU_LINK_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000 export SPU_LINK_RECV_TIMEOUT_MS = 600000 export SPU_LINK_HTTP_MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE = 4194304 export SPU_LINK_MAX_RETRY = 10 export SPU_LINK_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS = 1000 export SPU_LINK_MAX_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS = 10000 Check or remove the WAN configuration with: tc qdisc show dev lo sudo tc qdisc del dev lo root Required Source Code Modifications (Crucial) To reproduce the exact results reported in the paper (for the Join-MM-64 benchmarks), the following manual change to the underlying framework kernel is required: Please open the following file: Join-OSE/spu/src/libspu/kernel/hal/permute.cc (around Line 1026) Change from: bv_size = 32; Change to: bv_size = 64; How to Run Prerequisite: Clear the Bazel Cache Before running the benchmarks, we highly recommend clearing the Bazel cache to prevent any potential build conflicts from leftover historical files: bazel clean --expunge 1. summary: This article introduces Generative Relational Economics (GRE) as a preliminary research programme rather than a completed economic theory. Its starting point is historical. Modern economics developed under conditions in which scarce resources were commonly allocated among comparatively stable entities such as persons, households, firms, and states. Those abstractions remain indispensable, but contemporary transformations increasingly expose their limits. Globalized production, digital platforms, and artificial intelligence alter the scarcity of symbolic production, knowledge, and productive intelligence while many mechanisms of livelihood, recognition, and resource access remain tied to employment and comparative capability. AI also destabilizes inherited assumptions about the economic subject and makes persistent capability asymmetry difficult to ignore: human and artificial subjects may coexist under differences of knowledge, prediction, coordination, and productive capacity that are neither easily eliminable nor necessarily desirable to eliminate. The resulting problem is not asymmetry alone, but how it is converted through economic relations into dependency, exclusion, authority, resource concentration, or generative opportunity. GRE responds by shifting attention from allocation outcomes alone to the evolving relational structures through which resources and plural forms of value are generated, propagated, converted, recirculated, dissipated, and made capable of generating further possibilities. It does not reject entities, allocation, markets, or existing economics. It asks what becomes visible when entity-level interventions are also treated as relational interventions and when evaluation includes effects on future generative capacities. GRE draws on ontology and epistemology, aesthetics and epistemic orientation, relational and process thought, historical materialism, capability and care approaches, generative justice, and formal traditions in dynamical systems, complexity, networks, and fields. These traditions are treated as resources rather than collapsed into a single lineage. The article states GRE's disciplinary identity: its problem domain, characteristic questions, modes of inquiry, practical orientation, normative constraints, boundaries, and cumulative research programme. Its central proposal is that economics should ask not only who receives resources or what output follows, but what relational world an intervention helps generate, how value changes as it moves through that world, and how the intervention changes the conditions of subsequent generation. This statement remains deliberately programmatic and does not provide a complete formal model, a universal metric of generativity, or a final ontology of economic subjects and relations.
title: Towards Generative Relational Economics: A Preliminary Research Programme

summary: Production artificial intelligence systems are increasingly assessed not only by whether they generate accurate predictions, but by whether the operating organization can reconstruct, explain, and defend the exact evidence behind an individual outcome after the surrounding system has changed. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring that property, which we term evidence continuity. The framework is grounded primarily and foundationally in the work of Mesbaul Haque Sazu, specifically his Governed Decision-Intelligence (GDI) reference architecture [22] and his Full-Stack Production-Platform Reference Architecture [21]. GDI establishes the decision as the unit of assurance and makes evidence binding, lineage, validation, calibrated confidence, deterministic explanation, human oversight, and outcome closure explicit control obligations. The Full-Stack architecture extends these obligations into runtime operation through capture-at-commit, execution records, trajectory-level observability, before-commit gating, and closed-loop production control. Building directly on and leveraging these two foundations, this paper contributes a measurement layer that sits above them. We model an AI system as a typed, versioned, directed evidence graph and introduce three constructs: the Evidence Continuity Graph (ECG), the Trace Completeness Ratio (TCR), and the Governance Coverage Index (GCI). We formalize per-decision and aggregate estimators, extend the naive independence model to a correlated-failure regime using a Beta-Binomial mixture, and derive path-based reconstructability over admissible evidence paths. A synthetic benchmark of 2,800 investigation traces demonstrates how time-to-trace, incomplete-trace probability, and reconstruction probability respond as evidence coverage varies. The results are illustrative rather than empirical claims about deployed systems. The paper concludes with a reference implementation architecture, threshold-setting guidance calibrated to deployment risk, a security and failure analysis, and a research agenda for validating evidence continuity on real production workloads.

summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

summary: Structured quantum circuits are often represented by low-dimensional records such as occupation numbers or constraint feasibility rather than by full outcome distributions. A record loses control-dependent information when it merges outcomes whose probabilities respond differently to circuit parameters. We assess this loss without assuming a parametric hardware-noise model. Quantum Fisher information bounds premeasurement sensitivity; Fisher metrics of measurements and recorded statistics describe device-attainable sensitivity. For finite control changes, a Hellinger residual measures the response removed by a record, while its local quadratic term is the conditional covariance of the full-outcome score. Simultaneous confidence bounds support approval, refusal, or deferral. We prove a finite-library completion theorem: executable augmentations terminate either with a record preserving every declared response or with proof that no library augmentation removes the loss. For an analytic control germ, integral closures characterize preservation along every analytic control arc, and finitely many Rees valuations detect failure. This connects the state--measurement--record chain to an executable completion-or-refusal procedure, an attainable-Fisher kernel criterion, and finite-sample decisions. A three-qubit calculation separates measurement loss from record loss. Prospectively fixed IBM Kingston and Marrakesh experiments test decisions in four-qubit fixed-particle-number and GHZ families, including negative controls. In two-epoch IQM Garnet data, median record-level drift is 0.0797 times full-distribution drift, but a significant residual remains in 35 of 36 settings. On these circuits, the rules detect loss and approve records only within stated tolerances; they do not establish universal compression performance or device quantum Fisher information.
title: Completing or Refusing Low-Dimensional Records of Structured Quantum Circuits: Measurement Loss, Compression Loss, and Hardware Drift

summary: State-Dependent Ball-Screw Positioning Error Dataset: Operational Kinematic and ISO 230-2 Measurements Overview This dataset contains experimental positioning-error measurements acquired on a precision ball-screw-driven feed axis under systematically varied kinematic operating conditions. The dataset was generated using a dedicated automated test bench integrating servo-driven motion control, external laser interferometry with environmental compensation, distributed thermal monitoring, and automated data acquisition. The experimental campaign was designed to investigate positioning error beyond conventional static spatial characterization. In particular, the data enable positioning deviation to be analyzed as a state-dependent phenomenon influenced by the initial axis position, commanded displacement, preceding displacement, motion direction, reversal history, and motion velocity. Two complementary experimental datasets are provided: Operational kinematic measurements: acquired from independently sampled point-to-point movements over a broad range of kinematic states. Each experimental condition is defined as a batch and is repeated five times, with each repetition referred to as an action. ISO 230-2-based bidirectional positioning measurements: acquired under different spatial discretization and approach-velocity conditions, preserving the individual repeated measurements associated with each characterization curve. The operational dataset comprises two independent development campaigns containing a total of 2,000 distinct batches and an additional independent held-out evaluation campaign containing 300 batches . Since each batch was executed five times, the repository contains 10,000 action-level measurements for model development and 1,500 action-level measurements for independent evaluation. The ISO-based dataset contains 42 characterization curves resulting from seven spatial discretization values, three rotational velocities, and both motion directions. Individual experimental repetitions are preserved rather than providing only aggregated mean profiles. The repository therefore provides the experimental measurements required to reconstruct both the batch-level operational observations used for machine-learning modelling and the ISO-based spatial positioning-error profiles evaluated in the associated study. Associated Publication This dataset originates from the experimental campaign reported in the following manuscript, which should be consulted for the complete description of the experimental setup, measurement methodology, experimental design, positioning-error formulation, machine-learning framework, validation methodology, and ISO 230-2 analysis: Villoria-Ugidos, J., Martínez-Gutiérrez, A., Ferrero-Guillén, R., & Díez-González, J. Beyond Spatial Error Maps: Dynamic Modeling of Ball-Screw Positioning Error. Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing. Manuscript under review. DOI: to be added upon publication. Experimental Setup The experiments were carried out on a dedicated ball-screw feed-drive test bench specifically developed for the quantitative characterization of positioning error. The investigated transmission element is a precision-ground HIWIN R32-10K4-FSC ball screw with a nominal diameter of 32 mm, a nominal lead of 10 mm/rev, and tolerance class T3 according to DIN 69051 / ISO 3408. The total mechanical stroke of the experimental axis is approximately 750 mm. Axis actuation is provided by a Siemens SIMOTICS S-1FK7 servo motor operating in closed loop. The internal resolver feedback is used exclusively for motion control, while all positioning deviations reported in this dataset are evaluated using an external metrological reference. Linear displacement is measured using a Renishaw XL-80 laser interferometer equipped with an XC-80 environmental compensation unit . summary: This study develops the formulation of kinetic-energy manifestation within Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM) through a unified frequency–mass and phase-transformation framework. The analysis connects active matter-mass displacement, energy displacement, dual-frequency representation, phase-state transformation, and frequency-state evolution. The total frequency is represented as  f = fᵈᴮ + fᴾ , while the corresponding active mass displacement is represented through defined de Broglie and Planck contributions. The resulting energy displacement is expressed as  ΔPEᴇᴄᴍ = ΔKEᴇᴄᴍ = ΔMᴍc²  and connected with the proposed ECM frequency–energy correspondence  ΔKEᴇᴄᴍ = hf . The study then distinguishes energy representation from the transformation of the associated frequency state. The ECM phase-transformation relation  Tₓ° = x°/(360°f) = Δt  defines the transformation interval for the source or original frequency of the state undergoing transformation. The phase-state displacement  x°  is distinguished from the frequency displacement  Δf , while the ECM frequency-state sequence describes the transformation between pre-Planck, Planck, source, and observed frequency states. The formulation is further extended from a zero-phase origin to a general state-to-state transformation, yielding reciprocal phase–time and velocity–wavelength forms of the ECM transformation. An additional application develops the ECM interpretation of orbital telemetry phase residuals. The accumulated residual is represented through the source-frequency displacement  Δfꜱᴏᴜʀᴄᴇ , with the corresponding residual phase-state displacement represented by  x°res  and the accumulated telemetry residual by  ΔΦᴇᴄᴍ . This provides a proposed pathway from orbital motion through active mass–energy displacement, dual-frequency state formation, phase-state transformation, frequency-state displacement, and measurable phase residual. The formulation is presented as an internally organised ECM framework and does not claim, by itself, to constitute an experimentally established replacement for conventional mechanics or relativistic telemetry models.
title: Kinetic Energy in Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM): A Unified Phase–Frequency Transformation and Dynamical Manifestation

summary: This work supersedes v1.1 of this record. v1.0/v1.1 reported qualitative claims of numerical stability without a benchmark against a known solution, without a convergence study, and without a quantified account of the nonlocal-coupling limitation they identified in words. This version closes those three gaps. We benchmark the split-step Fourier (SSFM) implementation of the ESMA framework's logarithmic term against the exact "gausson" soliton solution of Bialynicki-Birula & Mycielski (1976), obtaining a fidelity of 1.000000000 and norm conservation to 3×10⁻¹³ for both a stationary and a Galilean-boosted soliton. A self-convergence study shows the numerical scheme converges at empirical order p ≈ 2.25 in the time step, consistent with the second-order Strang splitting used. We quantify the nonlocal coupling artifact identified in v1.1's original variance operator: two wave packets separated by 30 length units, with zero density overlap, show a spurious relative width shift ranging from the numerical noise floor (~10⁻⁹) at locality scale l ≤ 3 up to 7×10⁻² at l = 20, while the local gradient-based extension (β term, see the companion "Local Nonlinear Extension" record, 10.5281/zenodo.19110642 concept) remains at the noise floor independent of separation. Note: a duplicate of this file was briefly and mistakenly published under a different record's version history (10.5281/zenodo.19225060 concept, v2); that copy has been given matching corrected metadata and cross-references this one.
title: Numerical Validation of the ESMA Framework: Benchmark Against the Bialynicki-Birula–Mycielski Gausson, Convergence Analysis, and Quantified Nonlocal Coupling

summary: This software implements a  Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN)  for predicting cutting-tool flank wear and remaining useful life (RUL) on the  PHM2010 milling dataset . The network is built on an LSTM architecture in which the physical constraint derived from the  Archard wear equation  is embedded into the training loss: Ltotal = Ldata + λ·Lphysics where  Ldata  is the data-fitting mean squared error between the predicted and measured wear, and  Lphysics  penalizes the residual between the predicted wear rate and the Archard theoretical wear rate ( dVB/dt = k·Fn·Vt/H ). The pipeline first extracts time-domain statistical features from the 50 kHz sensor signals per cutting pass, then builds sliding-window sequences over the cutting order and feeds them to the LSTM for wear regression. It also includes a pure data-driven LSTM baseline for comparison. Requirements:  MATLAB R2024a (64-bit) with the Deep Learning Toolbox. See  REQUIREMENTS.md  for full software/hardware requirements. Run  tool_wear_pinn.m  for the PINN version and  tool_wear_phm2010.m  for the LSTM baseline;  check_pinn.m  provides a standalone self-test with synthetic data (no dataset files needed). Citation: If you use this software in your research, please cite it via its Zenodo DOI (see README). Source code for the algorithm proposed in the manuscript paper (Title: A Method for Predicting Tool Remaining Useful Life Based on a Physics-Informed Neural Network).
title: PINN-based Tool Wear Prediction on the PHM2010 Dataset

summary: The architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry has long struggled with a fundamental tension: generative design tools are exceptionally capable of producing vast solution spaces, yet they remain largely indifferent to whether those solutions can actually be built. Constructability considerations – site conditions, material logistics, structural sequencing, regulatory compliance – are typically addressed only after design alternatives have been generated, at which point revision is costly and disruptive. The result is a persistent misalignment between design ambition and construction reality. This paper proposes a conceptual vision and theoretical framework aimed at dissolving this boundary. Rather than treating constructability as a downstream filter, the framework reconceives it as an active participant in the generative process itself – a form of embedded construction intelligence that shapes design alternatives as they emerge, not after the fact. Design generation and construction reasoning, in this view, are not sequential but co-evolving. To support this vision, the framework conceptualizes three AI modalities working in concert. Generative design models drive the exploration of the solution space. Computer vision provides contextual grounding, interpreting site conditions and spatial configurations that abstract models would otherwise overlook. Natural language processing mines unstructured construction documents – specifications, codes, procedural guidelines – to surface the regulatory and practical knowledge that typically lives outside the model. Together, these components operate within a feedback loop that continuously interrogates and reshapes design candidates against constructability criteria. A key conceptual contribution of the work is what the authors term a "constructability-aware generative loop" – a design search process in which construction knowledge does not simply constrain outputs but actively guides the trajectory of exploration. Alongside this, the framework incorporates explainability as a core design principle rather than an afterthought. The system is conceptualized to communicate why a design was reshaped, giving practitioners meaningful insight into the trade-offs navigated between creative possibility and physical feasibility. To demonstrate the operational mechanics of this theoretical framework without asserting an empirical software deployment, an illustrative conceptual case study is presented using synthetic baseline parameters. Taken together, these elements represent a paradigm shift in how the field might approach early-stage design: not as an open-ended generative exercise followed by a feasibility check, but as an informed, context-sensitive process in which construction intelligence is present from the first iteration.
title: Beyond Form: Integrating Constructability As A Generative Driver Through Multimodal AI
