summary: The article “The Image of Istanbul in the Russian Émigré, Soviet, and Modern Russian-Language Literature” explores various facets of the city’s image through the lens of the short stories and essays of the first wave of Russian émigrés’ literature, Soviet literary work of the 1920s-1930s, and contemporary Russian-language Azerbaijani prose. Literary works by Nadezhda Teffi Istanbul and the Sun (1921) and Gaito Gazdanov A Weak Heart (1927) explored in the article, focus on the émigré experience representing two most common ways of depicting Istanbul among the Russian émigré writers. Teffi neither succumbs to Orientalist fantasy nor reduces the city to a refugee misery, she supports both notions and considers Istanbul to be the city of exiles’ humiliation and artistic transcendence, whereas Gazdanov interprets the first center of Russian emigration more clearly and tragically, depicting it as a symbol of life without any moral support. Soviet literature portrays Istanbul in an entirely different manner. During the 1920s-1930s, the description of the East was ideologically justified as it implicitly prepared the ground for developing the internationalist theme of “the friendship of peoples”. Thus, Soviet writers focused mainly on the political, social, and cultural changes which occurred in Turkey during the 1920s, highlighting the country’s transformation from a historical enemy to potential ally. Sweet Salt of the Bosphorus (2008) by a contemporary Azerbaijani author Elchin Safarli who takes into account the artistic experience of Russian émigrés, creates a transcultural space that exhibits the following features of transliterary writing: the author’s specific bilingual linguistic consciousness, the reconstruction of an Azerbaijani worldview through the Russian language, an interlinguistic textual field, the foregrounding of the cultural integration of Russians in the East and an objective reconstruction by the writer, who belongs to the Eastern cultural code, of a “Russian” perspective on the world.
title: Image of Istanbul in the Russian émigré, Soviet, and modern Russian-language literature

summary: Administrative registers of missing persons routinely produce three types of outcomes that conventional descriptive statistics treat as if they were one: cases with no outcome yet (genuine indeterminacy, characteristic of an ongoing search process), cases with an explicit negative outcome (for example, a report that was retracted or dismissed), and cases in which two extracts or two operational definitions of the same register yield incompatible figures. This article takes as its case study the missing-persons register of Ecuador's Ministry of the Interior, already documented and corrected in a previous round of factual auditing, and reframes it as a textbook example of what we call typed abstention: the formal distinction between "not on record" (no outcome has been recorded yet), "recorded as negative" (explicit denial), and "evidence conflict" (sources or definitions that do not match). Using the real, already-verified data - 4,892 records as of the August 19, 2026 extract, with 3,485 resolved cases (71.2%) and 1,407 under investigation (28.8%), against 4,507 records and the 742/3,528/237 breakdown (under investigation/located alive/deceased) of the July extract - we show that the 385-record discrepancy between extracts and the disparity among the 78.28%, 83.54%, and 71.2% resolution rates are not errors but instances of exactly the three types of indeterminacy that the evidential-reasoning literature (Dempster-Shafer theory, AGM belief revision, Belnap-Dunn four-valued logic) has been formalizing for decades with tools native to that tradition. We complement the analysis of the real data with an illustrative simulation study - explicitly synthetic, not derived from the real register - that quantifies, through 20,000 synthetic cases and 100 Monte Carlo replicates per scenario, how much of the aggregate gap between two extracts of the same register can be explained by asymmetric underreporting without any real contradiction between the sources, and how much information is lost when a binary "resolved/unresolved" scheme collapses genuine indeterminacy and negative closure into a single ambiguous category. The simulation results show that an underreporting asymmetry of just 10 to 20 percentage points between two extracts can produce aggregate gaps of 6.8 to 13.6 percentage points in the observed resolution rate - of the same order of magnitude as the real 12.3-percentage-point gap in the resolution rate between the July and August 2026 extracts - without either source being objectively wrong. We conclude that explicitly typing these three states, rather than collapsing them, improves the interpretability of public indicators without requiring complex inferential statistics or assumptions about the causes of the phenomenon.
title: Not on Record, Recorded as Negative, or in Conflict: Typed Abstention in Ecuador's Administrative Register of Missing Persons (2026)

summary: Administrative disability registries record certified cases, not disability as such: a person absent from the registry may lack certification because no certifiable impairment exists, because access to an evaluation board was unavailable, or because an evaluation is pending - three epistemically distinct situations that a single observed count cannot, by itself, distinguish. This paper reframes a nationwide descriptive analysis of Ecuador's National Disability Registry (Registro Nacional de Discapacidades, CONADIS/MSP; cut-off December 2023; N = 113,203 aggregated records representing 480,776 certified persons across 222 province-canton units) as an instance of typed abstention applied to administrative subregistration. We distinguish "not registered" (no consta: absence of a positive record, uninformative about the underlying condition) from a hypothetical "registered negative" (consta que no: an explicit denial after evaluation, a state that exists within the underlying certification process but is not exposed in the published open-data resource used here) and from internally conflicting evidence. Data quality auditing verified 100% structural completeness across all eight operational fields. The demographic and clinical profile shows a predominance of males (56.48%), adults aged 51 years and older (47.13%), physical disabilities (44.87%), and moderate impairment severity (45.78%). Guayaquil and Quito concentrate 30.83% of absolute registration volume, yet fall to the 134th and 144th of 221 population-normalized ranks, below the national median. Because the published registry cannot, by construction, separate certification capacity from underlying need, we add an illustrative synthetic simulation in which two data-generating mechanisms - pure certification-capacity heterogeneity and pure prevalence heterogeneity, each confounded with population size - produce observable correlations between the normalized rate and population that differ by only 0.021 (Pearson r = 0.949 vs. 0.928) despite sharing no causal mechanism, formalizing why the normalized rate cannot be read as need without an explicit, currently unavailable, capacity signal. We situate this identification problem within the literature on disability statistics (the Washington Group on Disability Statistics; the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health), administrative and missing-data quality, and evidential reasoning frameworks for typed indeterminacy (Dempster-Shafer belief functions, three- and four-valued logics, AGM belief revision), none of which have previously been applied to a cantonal-level disability registry of this kind.
title: Typed Abstention in Administrative Disability Registries: Certification Intensity, Subregistration, and the Limits of Cantonal Normalization in Ecuador's National Disability Registry (2023)

summary: This dataset supports the study “UDDPG-Net: Energy- and Fairness-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation in Underwater Communication Networks.” It contains the simulation data, experimental results, and lake-based acoustic measurement records used for evaluating UDDPG-Net. The simulation data cover underwater acoustic propagation, mobility, interference, energy states, resource-allocation decisions, training configurations, benchmark comparisons with Random, Greedy, PPO, TD3, SAC, MADDPG, and DDPG-GA, as well as scalability, ablation, exploration, SHAP, computational-efficiency, and robustness analyses. The field-test component corresponds to six campaigns conducted in Fengquan Lake, Xinxiang, China, and includes environmental, motion, acoustic-channel, and packet-level variables such as water temperature, salinity, pH, conductivity, sound speed, ambient-noise PSD, link distance, subband SNR, propagation delay, Doppler shift, and packet reception ratio. Reconstructed raw-format field logs are additionally provided to reproduce the organization and statistical characteristics reported in the manuscript; these files are clearly identified as reconstructed records and should not be interpreted as original instrument acquisition files. README files and structured metadata are included to describe the variables, units, experimental conditions, and correspondence between the released data and the figures and tables in the paper.
title: UDDPG-Net: Energy- and Fairness-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation in Underwater Communication Networks

summary: xinvert v0.3.0 Complete CUDA GPU back-end, a rename pass on the module and public API, and a thread-safe progress reporter. This release also folds in everything that had accumulated since v0.2.0 — v0.2.1 and v0.2.2 were developed but never published, so 0.3.0 is the next version on PyPI after 0.2.0. (Earlier gaps exist in this project too: 0.1.4–0.1.6 were tagged but never released.) Highlights GPU back-end for every equation type architect='gpu' now works for all seven solvers, not just the standard 2-D Poisson case: | equation type | CPU kernel | GPU kernel | | --- | --- | --- | | standard 1D | invert_standard_1D | invert_standard_1D_gpu | | standard 2D | invert_standard_2D | invert_standard_2D_gpu | | standard 2D full (flux form) | invert_standard_2D_full | invert_standard_2D_full_gpu | | standard 3D | invert_standard_3D | invert_standard_3D_gpu | | general 2D | invert_general_2D | invert_general_2D_gpu | | general 3D | invert_general_3D | invert_general_3D_gpu | | general 2D biharmonic | invert_general_bih_2D | invert_general_bih_2D_gpu | Red-Black SOR kernels with a shared loop skeleton ( _run_sor_2d_loop , _run_sor_3d_loop ), adaptive convergence-check intervals, and an optional per-call thread-block shape via iParams['gpu_block2d'] . GPU solves are bounded to one at a time ( gpus._GPU_MAX_CONCURRENT ) so dask can pipeline disk I/O against them, and CUDA context creation is done on the main thread. Measured on an RTX 3090: single timestep, 300 x 720: 17.3x (1.73 s GPU vs 29.99 s on one core) 12 timesteps, 300 x 720: ~1.6x over 12-core dask CPU (21.3 s vs 33.3 s) — at this size the solve is launch-bound, not execution-bound large grids, fixed 1000 iterations: up to 17.1x See the benchmark docs for the full sweep and the launch-overhead analysis. Module rename: numbas.py → cpus.py The CPU kernel module is now named for what it contains. xarray 's dask backend remains the multi-core path. API renames (breaking) Four public names lose a _test suffix that misdescribed them as test-only — they implement real discretizations used by shipped applications: | old | new | | --- | --- | | invert_standard_2D_test | invert_standard_2D_full | | inv_standard2D_test | inv_standard2D_full | | invert_GillMatsuno_test | invert_GillMatsunoFlux | | invert_Stommel_test | invert_StommelFlux | Users calling the old names must update; there are no aliases. The private __coeffs_*_test helpers became __coeffs_*Flux . Thread-safe live progress output printInfo output from dask worker threads and distributed clusters no longer interleaves. Each message is emitted as a single atomic write with the right parent header, so Jupyter and worker logs stay readable. Tests Seven CPU/GPU consistency suites ( tests/test_Gpu*.py plus tests/test_CpuGpuConsistency.py , ~1700 lines) asserting the analytic solution where one exists and CPU/GPU agreement otherwise; GPU cases skip cleanly when no CUDA device is present. Benchmark suite under tests/ , with machine-readable results in tests/results/*.json and figure regeneration via tests/plot_benchmarks.py . CI matrix: Python 3.9 – 3.12, 38 passed, 37 skipped . Housekeeping .gitattributes line-ending policy plus a one-off renormalization — the repository had a CRLF/LF mix that inflated diffs by thousands of lines. deriv() with the central scheme no longer converts numpy-backed input to dask; the rechunk is applied only to genuinely chunked data. Documentation: GPU status table, benchmark page and the parallel-inversions notebook brought in line with the implementation. Upgrade notes Breaking: the four API renames above. CUDA support is optional — import xinvert still works on machines without a GPU, and architect='cpu' remains the default. If you pin gpu_block2d , the default is still (16, 16) . Full diff: https://github.com/miniufo/xinvert/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0
title: xinvert: A Python package for inversion problems in geophysical fluid dynamics

summary: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Distinct conformational and interaction signatures of the FGFR1 V561M and N546K resistance-associated mutations: a multi-replicate molecular dynamics study" . This package contains everything needed to regenerate every table, figure and reported number in the manuscript from the analysis outputs, except the raw trajectories. Systems and sampling: three FGFR1 kinase domain systems (wild type, V561M, N546K) in complex with erdafitinib, three independent 500 -ns replicates each , analysed over the 200 -500 ns plateau. Nominal sampling 4.5 us; realised aggregate production sampling 4.491 us. All three systems share a 9.28387 nm cubic SPC water box with 0.15 M NaCl (total atoms 78 , 608 / 78 , 609 / 78 , 624 ). Contents: - scripts/ - 14 analysis and plotting scripts (Python 3.10 ) covering every main and supplementary figure panel - tables/ - 38 per-replicate and summary result tables (CSV) - matrices/ - 24 DCCM matrices, common-subspace PCA projections and RMSD series (NumPy .npy) - mdp/ - GROMACS run-control files (minimisation, ions, NVT, NPT, production) plus the fully expanded grompp parameter file - tpr/ - the nine production run inputs (complete, with all parameters baked in ) - topology/ - GROMACS topology files ( system and protein topologies, posre.itp, ligand parameters, index files ) - README.md - directory layout, frame-selection rules, uncertainty conventions, table/figure provenance, and full run parameters Software: GROMACS 2024.6 (production) and 2024.3 (analysis), gmx_MMPBSA 1.6 .5 , MDTraj 1.10 .3 , Python 3.10 (NumPy 2.2 .6 , SciPy 1.15 .2 , Matplotlib). Frame selection: MM/GBSA and MM/PBSA energies were computed on frames extracted at 1-ns spacing ( 301 frames per intact replicate ; 291 for V561M replicate 2 ). Replicate-level statistics use one value per independent trajectory ( n = 3 per system ) and are reported as mean +/- SD ; frames within a trajectory are not treated as independent samples . Per-residue decomposition values are reported as mean +/- SEM , which can be converted to SD by multiplying by the square root of 3 . Important for regeneration: the production runs were executed as a 200 -ns run followed by a 300 -ns extension (gmx convert -tpr -extend). md.mdp therefore defines only the first 200 ns and must be read together with that extension step. See README.md section 7. Raw trajectories (approximately 13 GB, full atom resolution, 100 -ps output cadence) are available from the corresponding author on request .
title: Reproducibility package for: Distinct conformational and interaction signatures of the FGFR1 V561M and N546K resistance-associated mutations: a multi-replicate molecular dynamics study

summary: This dataset is the frozen, reproducible evidence package supporting the manuscript Value Flow Mechanics for Mining Optimization through the LUJO Protocol. It links the version 1.1 manuscript, claim ledger, limitations, figures, tables, provenance records, and cryptographic manifests. summary: Code and data supporting the article "Capillary-driven networks obey Murray's law everywhere except at the meniscus". The archive contains three things. A self-contained MATLAB package that builds the figures of the article and recomputes every number quoted in its text, using a backtracking Newton iteration on a scale-invariant objective and requiring no toolboxes. A Python module that carries the same model on arbitrary graphs, including graphs with loops, where the flow is obtained from the nodal Laplacian rather than from the topology, together with a script that runs the verifications of Appendices C, F and H: the nine-channel graph with four independent loops, the envelope identity, the sweep over the driving degree, the three terminal conditions, the power-to-cost ratios and the Kamiya-Togawa law, and the case of several dissipation mechanisms in one channel. And a pixel-level digitisation of Fig. 7 of Zhang and Lorente, Sci. Rep. 13, 11278 (2023), against which Sec. V of the article is compared, with the source raster, the recovered coordinates in three formats, and an image comparing the reconstruction against the original. Neither optimiser uses the sizing law under test: each maximises the throughput at fixed cost from the resistance and the cost directly, so the residuals reported are an independent check of Eq. (7) rather than a restatement of it. The digitiser is deterministic and reproduces its 298 recovered points byte for byte. Code is released under the MIT licence (LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.txt). The source raster in data/ is reproduced unaltered from a CC BY 4.0 third-party article and remains copyright of its authors; see THIRD-PARTY.txt. summary: This work studies whether internal rotation changes the longevity of source-free localized excitations in the reduced Enchan local time-rate field. The frozen scalar dynamics are S_tt = div[mu(D) grad S] - S with D = |grad S| and mu(D) = 1/(1 + D^(3/2)); no continuing external torque, centrifugal force, primitive matter source, or added rotational potential is used during the reported evolutions. Stage A supplies the non-rotating source-free baseline. Stage B1 initializes rotating phase-space states at omega = 4, 8, and 12 and evolves the extended runs to dimensionless time t = 100. Over 80 <= t <= 100, the mean localized-energy fractions are approximately 0.002207 for the non-rotating baseline and 0.006006, 0.149470, and 0.368846 for omega = 4, 8, and 12. The result is a graded rotation-associated longevity hierarchy: weak rotation gives little practical rescue, intermediate rotation substantially extends localization, and the strongest tested branch remains transient-localized through t = 100. Matched-energy near-zero-J_z controls provide a separate causality check and show that net canonical angular momentum alone is not a monotonic explanation of every late-time difference. Stage B2 separately tests spontaneous self-spin from exactly zero initial total angular momentum and finds no validated convergent counter-rotating branch in the tested scalar-only initial-data families. The ordered scan supports a physical formation picture in which a localized grain can move from weak rotational asymmetry through progressive spin-up into a strong-rotation long-lived branch. Time, space, and omega are dimensionless reduced-branch quantities; t = 100 is not assigned an SI duration in this work. The deposit contains the Version 1.0 manuscript PDF, a reproducibility ZIP with the publication source, code, selected archived numerical outputs, README, LICENSE, and SHA-256 integrity manifest. The final main.pdf is the default preview. License: Enchan Research & Verification License v1.0. Copyright (c) 2026 Mitsuhiro Kobayashi.
title: Can Rotation Make Spacetime Grains Last? Internal Angular Momentum and Longevity of Source-Free Enchan Grains

summary: README – Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics (CGMD) Simulations of PIEZO1 and TRPM4 Overview This dataset contains coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and the non-mechanoprotective ion channel TRPM4 embedded in lipid bilayers. The simulations comprise 500 ns of equilibrium followed by membrane stretching simulations designed to investigate how PIEZO1's distinctive triskelion blade architecture redistributes mechanical stress and preserves membrane integrity. All simulations were performed using GROMACS with the Martini 3 force field. Independent replicate simulations (n = 3) were conducted for each system to ensure statistical robustness and reproducibility. Simulation Details Parameter Description Molecular dynamics engine : GROMACS v2021.2 Force field : Martini 3 Membrane model : Lipid bilayer containing either PIEZO1 or TRPM4 Equilibration : 500 ns Stretching simulations : Three independent replicates (n = 3); 50 ns Simulation temperature, pressure, and all additional parameters are provided in the accompanying simulation input files (.mdp) and described in the associated publication. Biological Significance PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive ion channel whose unique triskelion blade architecture protects cellular membranes from mechanical failure. Its extended peripheral blades redistribute mechanical stress across the lipid bilayer, reducing localized stress accumulation and delaying membrane rupture during mechanical loading. This dataset enables quantitative investigation of how membrane protein architecture influences membrane mechanics, force redistribution, and mechanoprotection using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Dataset Structure 1. Equilibrium Simulations These simulations characterize the equilibrated membrane environment surrounding each ion channel before mechanical loading. Simulation length: 500 ns PIEZO1_equilibrium.pdb PIEZO1_equilibrium.xtc TRPM4_equilibrium.pdb TRPM4_equilibrium.xtc 2. Membrane Stretching Simulations Following equilibration, membrane stretch was induced using semi-isotropic pressure coupling, with −5 bar applied in the membrane plane (x–y) while maintaining +1 bar normal to the bilayer (z-axis) using the Parrinello–Rahman barostat. title: PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress using MD simulation

summary: Industry 4.0 transforms manufacturing through cyber-physical systems, the Industrial Internet of Things, digital twins, and data-driven intelligence, yet the volume of latency-sensitive data these technologies generate strains conventional cloud-only computing. Edge and fog computing have emerged as the central enabling paradigm, distributing computation across a device–fog–cloud continuum. This paper surveys the enabling technologies of Industry 4.0 with an emphasis on edge–cloud computing and formulates the resulting computation-offloading problem as a constrained, load-dependent optimization model that jointly minimizes task latency and device energy under deadline and capacity constraints. A genetic algorithm and a particle swarm optimizer are developed and benchmarked against five baseline strategies on synthetic industrial workloads. Across one hundred tasks averaged over ten instances, the genetic algorithm reduced the weighted objective by 34.1 percent relative to a greedy heuristic and by 82.6 percent relative to cloud-only execution, while lowering deadline violations to 1.6 percent. The latency–energy trade-off, convergence, and scalability are analyzed, and managerial implications for industrial deployment are discussed.
title: Energy- and Latency-Aware Computation Offloading in Edge–Fog–Cloud Architectures for Industry 4.0

summary: Supplementary material for the manuscript Li Bai Says Xiangsi and Du Fu Does Not: Idioms of Longing in Tang Poetry and the Lexical Basis of an Emotion Label by Zizheng Lv (Honours Program, Department of Asian Studies, University of British Columbia). The study asks what the yearning label of the Chinese Classical Poetry Dataset (CCPD) measures when a classifier trained on it rates Li Bai far above Du Fu. On held-out benchmark poems the label is recoverable from the words xiangsi (相思) and xiangyi (相忆); in a source-audited corpus of 52,253 Tang poems, xiangsi is followed as a formula with a history, from pre-Tang song to Tang poems of farewell and exchange, across 116 poets, and into fifteen close readings. Contents of Supplementary_Material.zip data/poems_table.parquet : the 52,253 author-eligible, CCPD-training-disjoint Tang poems (chinese-poetry, MIT) with source pointers, normalized and original bodies, poem families, surface forms, the frozen classifier's yearning probability and decision, per-poem counts of the words in the lexicon of longing, and title flags. data/author_dates.csv , data/author_dates_by_poem.csv , data/author_date_supplement.json : author dating for the Tang diachrony (Chinese Text Project Data Wiki plus listed corrections). data/xiangsi_poems_by_title_type.csv , data/dufu_yi_news_poems_by_title_type.csv : every title behind the title-type analyses with its rule-based type. data/literary_case_register.json : source-linked records for the fifteen readings. evidence/ : the numbers behind every figure and statement (benchmark counts and coefficients, corpus rates, lexicon rates with family-bootstrap intervals, diachrony, position, addressee, per-character logit attributions, form standardization, per-author tables for 116 poets, song-title rates). contextual_comparison/ : protocol and results of the three GuwenBERT fine-tuning runs. provenance/ : source versions, permissions, licenses, historical sources, and SHA-256 hashes of the archive inputs. scripts/ , figure_source/ : analysis and rendering code; requirements.txt lists the versions used. file_manifest.json and verify_results.py : SHA-256 integrity check for every distributed file (run python verify_results.py ). What runs from this package. scripts/b_e1_lexicon.py , scripts/d_e3_e4_e6.py and scripts/g_e7_all_poets.py recompute their evidence files from the distributed poem table, and figure_source/render_figures.py renders Figures 1 to 6 from the evidence files. scripts/c_e2_diachrony.py and scripts/h_e8_southern_song.py additionally require the Daizhige transcription of Lu Qinli's pre-Tang anthology and the CText Data Wiki RDF release; scripts/e_e5_attribution.py requires the fitted CCPD pipeline; scripts/a_build_table.py documents how the poem table was derived from the archive. These inputs are third-party or too large to redistribute; the README section External inputs gives their expected locations, and each script stops with a message naming any missing input. Licensing. The author's own contributions in this package (code, evidence files, the poem table's derived columns, the case register, and documentation) are released under CC BY 4.0. Retained third-party notices continue to apply to the respective upstream materials: the poem texts derive from the MIT-licensed chinese-poetry repository, whose notice is included; the birth and death years in data/author_dates.csv and data/author_dates_by_poem.csv derive from the Chinese Text Project Data Wiki and remain under its CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 license, with the author's corrections listed separately in data/author_date_supplement.json . summary: This paper offers a critical analysis of the European Union as a model of regional integration and examines its contribution to peace and to the effectiveness of the United Nations system. Set against the background of the failure of the League of Nations, the study argues that the post-1945 international order has endured largely because it is supported by strong regional institutions. Using the EU as the primary case study, the paper contends that by institutionalizing peace within Europe through economic interdependence, binding law, and supranational governance, the EU has created a zone of stability that reduces the burden on global governance structures. Furthermore, the paper analyzes how the EU functions as a support pillar for the United Nations under Chapter VIII of the UN Charter. Through financial contributions, peacekeeping partnerships, and coordinated diplomacy, the EU has reinforced multilateralism and provided capacity for conflict management and development. A comparative perspective is also drawn with other regional bodies such as ECOWAS to demonstrate a broader pattern of regional-global cooperation. The paper concludes that the longevity of the United Nations, compared to the League of Nations, can be partly explained by this two-level architecture of global and regional governance. While the EU’s support for the UN is substantial, it is also inconsistent, as internal EU divisions sometimes undermine collective action. Ultimately, the study shows that effective regional integration is a critical condition for sustaining peace and strengthening the United Nations system.
title: The European Union and Regional Integration: A Critical Analysis of Peacebuilding and Support for the United Nations System

summary: Abstract The stability of the banking sector is fundamental to economic growth and financial system resilience, particularly in developing economies such as Nigeria.  However, and sadly enough, global, recent and recurring failure risks and collapses of banks which have been blamed on poor external audit qualities, are counter-productive to national economic development.  Therefore, the broad objective of this study was to study the effect of audit quality on failure risks of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria between the period 2009 and 2024. This study adopted both descriptive and ex-post facto research designs.  Using secondary data extracted from audited financial reports of 11 censored (from a population of 11) deposit money banks listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group, (NGX), and analyzing one hundred and seventy-six firm year observations using regression with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors analysis technique, the findings revealed that audit firm size (AUFS) significantly improve bank Z score, [coef. = 0.638 (p-value = 0.005)], audit report timeliness (ARTIME) significantly reduces bank Z score [coef. = −0.400 (p-value = audit committee diligence (ACDI) revealed a positive insignificant effect respectively on Z score of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria during the period under consideration. Based on the above findings, it was concluded that audit quality in the Nigerian banking sector is not uniformly effective, rather, its effect on bank failure risks is selective, with only specific audit mechanisms demonstrating the capacity to significantly enhance financial solvency, thereby suggesting that the effectiveness of external audit as a safeguard against bank failure risks depend not merely on its presence, but likely on factors such as depth, credibility, and functional execution of its key components.   this study concluded that audit.  Consequently, this study recommended among others, that listed deposit money banks in Nigeria, alongside regulators and external auditors, should prioritize substantive governance quality, auditor competence and independence, rigorous audit execution, timely financial reporting, risk-sensitive audit remuneration, coordinated assurance mechanisms, and proactive internal control systems over mere procedural compliance, in order to strengthen transparency, reinforce market confidence, and enhance long term financial stability in line with Agency theory. Keywords: Audit Quality, Failure Risks of Listed Deposit Money Banks, Bank Z-Score, Agency Theory.

summary: Concern about low-information-content publications—least publishable units, salami-sliced outputs, redundant papers, benchmark increments, and false-positive findings dressed as discoveries—is distributed unevenly across the sciences. Some fields appear to convert procedural effort into publishable "findings" almost at will, whereas others force nearly every contribution into the slow form of a convergence result or an error audit. Existing accounts attribute the disparity to incentives, statistical flexibility, or disciplinary culture, but incentives are universal while the output pattern is not, and flexibility alone cannot explain fields whose verdicts are stringent and objective yet are gamed at industrial scale. This paper develops a structural account centered on two features of a research program: the closure of its decision space by formal and empirical constraints, and the gameability of the verdicts that adjudicate its claims. Stringency, fidelity to the epistemic target, and resistance to rehearsal are distinct properties of a verdict; a benchmark can be maximally stringent and objective while remaining trivially gameable. Because the underlying dimensions are ordinal and non-compensatory, susceptibility to low-information publication cannot be expressed as a scalar ratio and is better represented as a typology. Four regimes are distinguished: convergent programs with dual closure and ungameable verdicts; formally bounded programs with thin empirical closure; programs governed by stringent but gameable verdicts; and open-latitude programs with weak closure and subjective adjudication. Each regime channels publication pressure into a different production line—flexibility monetization, verdict gaming, or fragmentation and repackaging—and each requires interventions matched to its production line rather than a generic reform package. The model explains why string theory and fixed-benchmark machine learning, often misread by single-axis accounts, exhibit such different pathologies, and it predicts which reforms will work, fail, or backfire in each regime.
title: The Structural Determinants of Low-Information Publication in Science: A Constraint–Verdict Typology

summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

summary: Embarrassingly parallel workloads, such as parameter sweeps, Monte Carlo simulations, and hyperparameter searches, are pervasive in research computing, yet running a single experiment across a mix of laptops, lab servers, cloud virtual machines (VMs), and high-performance computing (HPC) clusters still demands ad hoc Secure Shell (SSH) tunnels, port forwarding, and scheduler-specific scripts. We present DART, a job distributor that turns any such mix of machines into a single shared queue. DART pairs a Dockerized job server with a one-line worker command-line interface (CLI); a hosted Hub automates reverse tunneling, worker authentication, and public endpoint provisioning, so collaborators on any network, including those behind network address translation (NAT) or using a personal laptop, can join an experiment with a single API-key and no firewall changes. This makes DART especially effective for researchers who combine Advanced Cyberinfrastructure Coordination Ecosystem: Services & Support (ACCESS)-provisioned HPC resources [1] with institutional clusters and personal workstations, federating all resources under one queue with no per-site configuration. All communication is encrypted end-to-end, and access is controlled through API-key authentication and a personal identification number (PIN)-protected dashboard. Researchers create experiments, define parameter grids, and monitor jobs entirely from a web dashboard; a work-conserving scheduler dispatches jobs on demand, exploits resource heterogeneity, and automatically re-queues failures. In a real-world deployment of 37,720 jobs across 68 heterogeneous machines spanning an institutional HPC cluster, a national ACCESS resource, and personal computers, the observed run completed in approximately eight days. DART’s dynamic allocation achieved a simulation-derived 35× speedup over static partitioning (≈4 days vs. ≈139 days), reducing a multi-month workload to days.
title: DART: Distributed Assignment of Research Tasks for Heterogeneous Compute Environments

summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. Files: main.pdf contains the main article (14 pages); supplement.pdf contains the supplementary proofs and additional results (33 pages). Related Lean verification sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22554594 and https://github.com/HongruZhao/ComplexGramHafnians.
title: Local Anticoncentration for Gaussian Boson Sampling via Conditional Wishart Geometry

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Eighteen entries are documented, eight of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, and converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient.
title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

summary: Research and educational instrument. Not for clinical use, for the care of any patient, or to determine or influence any drug dose. A simulation-calibrated informatics pipeline that fits a single-compartment exponential approximation to published population pharmacokinetic models of unfractionated heparin during cardiopulmonary bypass, and renders the result as an institution-specific decay nomogram. This is the supporting code and archived analysis for manuscript JCVA-D-26-01511. Published models of heparin disposition are biexponential and require a computer to evaluate. The pipeline asks how well a single decay constant k — calibrated to an institution's own dosing, weight and bypass-time distributions — can approximate a chosen reference model, and quantifies where it fails. The answer differs sharply by model: at the reversal timepoint the approximation holds to 0.38% mean absolute error for Lanoiselée and 0.44% for Jia, but to 10.3% for Delavenne, rising to 72% after repeated supplemental boluses. Contents. Five reference-model implementations with their published parameters and provenance; seeded cohort sampling and calibration; agreement statistics; nomogram geometry and rendering; a Streamlit dashboard; an automated test suite; and a frozen analysis run comprising 20 result tables, the main-text and supplementary figures, a run manifest and a manuscript-ready summary. A sixth model (PRODOSE-2) is implemented and tested but withheld from the active pipeline pending validation and peer review. Reproduction. Every reported number regenerates from one seeded command: pip install -r requirements-frozen.txt python run_analysis.py --seed 20260912 --outdir /tmp/check python check_frozen.py /tmp/check All randomness comes from explicitly seeded generators, each analysis stage drawing from its own independent stream. Re-running reproduces every archived result to within floating-point rounding on any machine, and byte-for-byte on the machine the archive was built on. The manifest records the seed, the commit, the package versions and every analysis decision. Continuous integration runs the suite on two Python versions, each test file again in isolation, and the reproduction check on every push. Verification, and its limits. Automated checks confirm that each closed-form solution actually solves its own differential equations and satisfies the identities they imply, and six landmark values from a published simulation are reproduced to within 3%. No participant-level data from any source study is held, so no model is re-fitted and no prediction is compared with an observation. What is demonstrated is faithful implementation of the published models — not that the published models are correct. No external or predictive validation is claimed. Scope. The pipeline represents the pharmacokinetic central-compartment amount only. It does not model the pharmacodynamic layer — anti-factor Xa activity or activated clotting time — nor peripheral-compartment heparin, antithrombin, protamine pharmacology or heparin rebound. Converting a residual amount into a protamine dose requires an institutional ratio that this software does not supply. Intended purpose. This software is a research and educational instrument whose purpose is to demonstrate and teach an informatics method under simulated conditions. Within that intended purpose it is not a medical device. Nothing here has been cleared, approved or evaluated by any regulatory authority; outputs have not been validated against measured anti-factor Xa activity, activated clotting time or clinical reversal in patients, and no clinical benefit has been demonstrated. Anyone using it outside the intended purpose does so on their own responsibility and may bring the tool within medical-device oversight in their jurisdiction; the authors accept no responsibility for such use. Version 2.0.0 changes every statistic reported by 1.x and corrects two errors in previou
title: Heparin decay nomogram pipeline

summary: Within the Complementarity-First and Reciprocal Internal Complementarity research program, we study regular perturbations of a supplied smooth massive degree-one SU(2) Yang–Mills–Higgs monopole with equal scalar and vector masses. A neutral transverse readout satisfies an exact nonlinear equation whose source is a divergence of an L2 tensor plus an L6/5 remainder. An additional affine infrared class is preserved on compact regular intervals and transported to admitted framed gauge and collective charts. Ordinary kinetic collective subtraction need not preserve its homogeneous negative norm; a compensating sum retains the relevant cancellation. Pure spatial transport is skew, while complete coordinate corrections admit an endpoint Duhamel identity. These statements concern finite-time admissibility, not uniform all-time localization. Assuming the companion’s nonnegative physical Hessian, complete framed kernel, local-moment coercivity and explicit threshold-packet estimates, a Gauss projection of a compact weighted translation yields a sharper test in the same monopole background. Its affine tail label differs from its actual initial local center rate, and its collective-orthogonal velocity lies outside the domain of the physical Hessian’s inverse square root. Its global linearized local-moment connection residual is unbounded in kinetic L2 while remaining bounded in the energy norm. We obtain an exponentially weighted time-average lower bound, not a universal pointwise growth law. Fixed-time differentiability excludes a time-uniform linear-scale nonlinear strong-residual estimate on this class, but does not establish nonlinear Lyapunov instability. The actual spectral inverse-square-root domain is necessary and sufficient for bounded unforced linear radiative position. We identify the nonlinear physical source that would need stronger control. The example proves that affine admissibility does not imply spectral admissibility; it does not classify their full inclusion relation or prove all-time nonlinear spectral propagation.
tags: Complementarity-First; Reciprocal Internal Complementarity; magnetic monopole; infrared control; affine tail class; spectral inverse domain; collective modulation; threshold wave; Lean.
title: Affine and Spectral Infrared Control of Monopole Perturbations

summary: This record contains the experimental reproducibility package accompanying the study “Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering.” The package provides the complete Jupyter notebook, generated figures, run-level results, aggregated summaries, parameter-sensitivity analyses, bootstrap-stability estimates, drift-response measurements, and paired statistical comparisons. The experimental evaluation compares Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), Possibilistic C-Means (PCM), Possibilistic Fuzzy C-Means (PFCM), and entropy-regularized FCM across five datasets: Iris, Wine, Breast Cancer Wisconsin, Digits represented by four unsupervised principal components, and an imbalanced overlapping synthetic dataset. The methods are evaluated under baseline conditions, Gaussian measurement noise, missing values followed by median imputation, and partial mean-shift drift. The full protocol uses ten paired random seeds, three initializations per fit, and twenty bootstrap resamples for each dataset–scenario–model combination. Class labels are excluded from model fitting and hyperparameter selection and are used only for external evaluation. The archive is organised into code, figures, and results directories. The notebook contains the complete workflow required to reproduce the reported experiments.
title: Experimental Reproducibility Package for "Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering"

summary: RED-2400 is a public benchmark of 6,660 algorithmically-rejected trading events drawn from a live Solana decentralised-exchange filter stack, observed continuously between 2026-04-10T21:10Z and 2026-05-02T21:48Z UTC (22 calendar days). The deposit contains 169,123 forward-outcome observations and 1,837 graveyard-tracker lifecycle snapshots covering 1,076 distinct mints in the rejection registry and 1,075 distinct mints in the forward-observation file. Linkage between rejection events and forward outcomes (corrected). Outcome linkage is available for approximately half of the benchmark events. Of 6,660 registry rejection events, 3,333 (50.0%) exactly match an outcome event key on (mint, timestamp, reason); 3,327 (50.0%) have no exact matched trajectory. At the mint level 1,075 of 1,076 registry mints (99.9%) appear at least once in `rejection_outcomes.csv`, so a mint-level join is near-complete even though the event-level join is not. A further 705 outcome-side event keys (17.5% of the 4,038 distinct outcome keys) correspond to rejection events that are not present in the registry, and 348 outcome rows are missing rejection reason or timestamp and cannot be joined back to a registry event on any key. Analyses requiring linked outcomes are restricted to the linked subset. The graveyard-tracker file supports external validation of any outcome-classification rule against observed token lifecycle. The tracker began emitting 13 calendar days after the rejection window opened; lifecycle observations for rejection events earlier than 2026-04-23T18:07Z are right-shifted by at least 13 days relative to the rejection. Mint-level presence in the tracker is 99.3% (1,068 of 1,076 registry mints). The true set difference |graveyard \ registry| equals 23 mints, and 8 registry mints are absent from the tracker.
title: RED-2400: A Public Benchmark of Algorithmically-Rejected Trading Events with Outcome Labels

summary: This work presents an efficient numerical technique for solving Fredholm integro-differential equations (FIDEs) using Laguerre polynomial basis functions. The proposed method transforms the given integro-differential equation into an equivalent integral form, which is subsequently approximated through the collocation technique at standard collocation points. The resulting system of algebraic equations is solved using matrix inversion procedures to obtain the approximate numerical solution. The existence, uniqueness, continuity, and convergence of the proposed method are established using the Banach fixed-point theorem. Three numerical examples covering first, second, and third-order FIDEs are solved to demonstrate the applicability, accuracy, and computational efficiency of the method. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves absolute errors ranging from 0.00 to 7.05 × 10⁻⁵ at truncation order N = 5, which are substantially smaller than those reported for existing methods. Specifically, for the first-order problem, the method produces exact solutions at all evaluation points, while for the second- and third-order problems, the maximum absolute errors are 7.05 × 10⁻⁵ and 0.00, respectively. These results confirm the superior accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed approach.
title: A Numerical Technique for Solving High-Order Fredholm Integro-Differential Equations Via Laguerre Polynomial Approximation

summary: Abstract Modern enterprise AI systems increasingly operate across multiple authorized data sources, memories, applications, and tools. This creates a security problem that is not adequately described as conventional data theft. An AI workload may be individually authorized to read support records, engineering information, source-control activity, supplier data, budgets, hiring information, and calendars. No individual source may contain a sensitive strategic conclusion. However, the AI system may combine those independently authorized fragments and reconstruct a new high-value object: an unreleased product direction, likely launch window, supplier dependency, market strategy, organizational weakness, or other forward-looking enterprise knowledge. The security boundary therefore changes. The relevant questions are no longer only: Who may read data A? or: Who may read data B? They also become: Who may establish the relationship A-to-B? Who may retain or disclose the resulting inference? Who may cause an external action because of that reconstructed meaning? This paper describes a threat model in which the AI assistant becomes a computational graph across previously separate enterprise systems. The resulting risk may exist even when each underlying retrieval complies with its ordinary source-level permissions. The sensitive object is not necessarily a stolen database record; it may be a new semantic object created through authorized association. The architecture therefore separates two security transitions: Authorized Data | v Authorized Reconstruction | v Computed Meaning | v Authorized Effectuation | v External Consequence The first transition concerns association authority : permission to read independently authorized fragments does not automatically imply permission to join those fragments into a new semantic relationship. The second concerns execution-time finality : permission to compute, generate, or prepare an output does not automatically imply permission for that output to become externally consequential. The proposed architectural model therefore introduces controls around independently governed relationship mapping, session-bound reconstruction, minimum-necessary temporary views, provenance-aware release, and a mandatory effectuation boundary. Candidate outputs or actions remain non-effective until the consequence-controlling component verifies the applicable authority, provenance, destination, policy state, disclosure conditions, and other protected execution state immediately before release or effectuation. In compact form: Access != Association Association != Authority to Disclose Computation != Authority to Cause Consequence The execution-time consequence boundary may be implemented through existing mechanisms such as policy-enforcement points, reference monitors, authorization servers, secure execution environments, transaction coordinators, capability systems, protected dispatchers, database commit controls, network command gates, or equivalent mechanisms. The important property is functional rather than terminological: A computed result or proposed action remains non-effective until the component with mandatory control over the actual consequence verifies that the exact pending effect is permitted under current protected authority and state. This architecture is intended to complement conventional identity, access control, encryption, zero-trust, data-loss prevention, confidential-computing, logging, and authorization systems rather than replace them. Those mechanisms continue to protect identities, stores, channels, and individual permissions. The additional problem addressed here is governance of the relationship created between authorized fragments and governance of the transition from computed meaning to actual consequence . The paper presents this as a forward-looking threat model rather than an allegation concerning any specific enterprise or AI product. The objective is to identify an architectural risk
title: Enterprise AI as a Reconstruction Layer: Governing Derived Knowledge and Execution-Time Consequences

summary: This paper proposes a persistent epistemic architecture for AI systems in which durable cognitive state is explicit and independent of any particular language model. The persistent substrate maintains inspectable, scoped beliefs with provenance, distinguishes individual sources and accumulates domain-sensitive trust, retains unresolved questions across interactions, and supports offline consolidation that detects contradictions and generates hypotheses. Its contents participate directly in subsequent learning and action rather than serving only as retrieved memory. A dependency-free prototype instantiates this core, with language models at both linguistic interfaces, to illustrate the cycle by which attributed testimony becomes revisable belief. The central claim is that continual learning requires explicit epistemic structure: a representation of what the system believes, why it believes it, whom it learned it from, and what remains unresolved, if its evolving epistemic state is to remain inspectable and correctable. This becomes increasingly consequential as AI systems contribute to their own development, because increasing capability does not necessarily entail a corresponding improvement in epistemic reliability. Persistent epistemic state provides a substrate on which correction and calibration can accumulate over time while remaining externally auditable. Preprint submitted to arXiv in September 2026. Source code and demonstrator: https://github.com/protopopescu/chloe and  https://lftm.gla.ac.uk/chloe/
title: CHLOE: A Persistent Epistemic Architecture for Inspectable AI

summary: We prove that a finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the following common-incomparability property has at most 48 antichains: for every x < y, the elements incomparable with both x and y form a chain of size at most two. An explicit fifteen-element poset attains the bound. We show that order-six stable-marriage rotation posets satisfy these hypotheses by examining convex rotation blocks and their fixed partner pools. This gives a structural upper bound of 48 stable matchings, matching the lower bound already provided by Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger in 1995. Equality forces fifteen rotations, all of size two, and every one of the 36 man–woman pairs occurs in some stable matching. Provenance note: This preprint is accompanied by reproducible verification artifacts and a partial Lean formalization. The Lean development verifies the finite-poset core and supporting components; it does not formalize the entire stable-marriage theorem f(6) = 48 end to end. The source-code and reproducibility repository is available at https://github.com/insammael/stable-marriage-f6 and is linked as a related resource.
title: Small Rotation Blocks and the Order-Six Stable Marriage Problem

summary: This report reconstructs the publication history of The Watermark, the student literary and arts journal of the University of Massachusetts Boston. It was published from 1993 through 2022 under that title. This report draws on physical copies, digital archival holdings from ScholarWorks and personally held hard copies, as well as firsthand research, it examines the journal's institutional and material history. It also documents changes in production and distribution, as well as gaps in the surviving digital record. The report concludes with a reconstructed record of known volumes and is periodized.
title: The Watermark (1993–2022): A Publication History and Reconstruction

summary: Science communication poster and educational resource developed for the 2026 European Researchers’ Night–Nit de la Investigació at the University of Alicante as supporting material for a hands-on activity devoted to coin production. For this activity, an enlarged minting system based on the dies of a silver Carthaginian shekel has been reproduced by means of 3D printing. Participants can directly experience how hammered coinage works by placing a modelling-clay flan between a fixed lower die and a movable upper die, and observing how pressure impresses the obverse and reverse types onto its surface. The poster provides the historical and technological context for this activity through an overview of the evolution of coin production and means of payment, from manual hammered coinage to the mechanisation of coin manufacture and contemporary digital payment systems. It presents in a synthetic way some of the main technological developments, including hammered coinage, mechanised roller minting, the screw press, banknote production and security features, and the progressive dematerialisation of payment methods. Developed within the framework of the PArchTE ( Predictive Archaeology and Transition Economies ) and SEDES (PID2023-152305NB-I00) projects. The activity forms part of “UA Divulga VI. Annual Plan of the UCC+i of the University of Alicante (2025–2026)” (FCT-24-20347), funded by the Spanish Foundation for Science and Technology (FECYT). Activity developed by the University Institute for Research in Archaeology and Historical Heritage (INAPH), University of Alicante.
title: Arqueología de la producción monetal

summary: Multi-agent active inference gives a natural account of belief sharing: agents hold local posteriors over a shared latent state, communicate those beliefs, and pool them into a colony-level consensus. The same mechanism is fragile when a member is miscalibrated, corrupted, or strategically wrong. Because the standard pool multiplies the reports together, a single confident-but-wrong broadcast that puts near-zero mass on the true state can pull the whole consensus off it, outweighing many honest members. The colony therefore needs a way to preserve the useful structure of belief sharing while limiting the influence of contaminated beliefs. This paper presents Active Fedference, a discrete-categorical framework that connects robust federated generalized variational inference with active inference belief sharing. The main bridge is structural: standard belief sharing appears as the non-robust corner of a broader generalized-Bayes family, while robust losses, conservative server fusion, and explicit aggregation diagnostics describe how the system moves away from that corner under declared contamination mechanisms. The result is not a replacement for belief sharing, but a containment result: ordinary belief sharing is recovered when robustness is turned off. Bounded-loss theory applies on the client axis, while the variational-server axis supplies an objective-backed redescending weight update. Following the manuscript's authoritative three-axis guarantee map, the paper keeps source-conditional client updates, a recovery-only heuristic server rule, and an objective-backed variational server rule as separate claim owners, with no robustness guarantee transferred between them. The study suite then exercises the framework as an end-to-end research system: recovery checks anchor the standard-Bayes limit, belief-sharing studies verify the communication baseline, contamination experiments test robust consensus, and extension studies probe moving agents, hierarchical latent structure, sensitivity to acuity and colony size, parameter recovery, and single-host socket-backed federation traces. All reported quantities are generated from deterministic analysis artifacts and injected into the manuscript by token, so the paper, figures, release package, and validation reports remain tied to the same execution record. The open-source repository is ActiveInferenceInstitute/Active_Fedference. This final-release manuscript uses assigned version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22149133; the bound deposited PDF and repository release are controlled by separate publication gates.
title: Robust Belief Sharing in Federated Active Inference: A Recovery-Tested Generalized-Variational Framework for Categorical Contamination-Aware Consensus

summary: Recent agentic campaigns show that coordinated AI systems can compress reconnaissance, exploitation, and credential harvesting into machine-tempo operations. This paper asks a narrow question: whether increasing the number of untrusted attack sources changes the authorization outcome of an inline control that mediates every protected path and permits only explicit device-to-device relations. Under stated assumptions of complete mediation, fixed and correct policy, uncompromised trust anchors, no alternate path, and sufficient enforcement capacity, it does not. Additional untrusted source identities create additional denied first-contact events, not a permitted relation. This is a conditional property of the authorization rule, not a claim that throughput, alert volume, or availability are independent of swarm size. A four-run laboratory test of an AutoGen agent using GPT-4o provides a mechanism demonstration: the agent created four fresh network identities, and each was denied at its first observed unauthorized probe. The test does not establish a population rate or current-frontier performance. A closed-form illustration shows why reconnaissance opportunity grows with total probe volume when no relation enforcement exists, while the authorization outcome remains denial under the stated assumptions. Residual risks include fingerprinting, compromise of a trusted endpoint, policy error, incomplete path coverage, implementation bypass, and resource exhaustion. Detection remains necessary for evidence and follow-on response; the narrower claim is that alert-only detection should not be the primary containment mechanism for a machine-tempo campaign.
title: The AI Agent Swarm Meets First Contact: Conditions Under Which Preventive Relation Enforcement Is Scale-Invariant

summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

The reproduction command stages the archived routes, regenerates downstream tables and copies the included figure assets. A full routing rerun additionally requires the externally distributed Natural Earth 10 m v5.1.1 and GSHHG 2.3.7 full L1 coastline datasets. Tests and release checks are documented in the archive. The comparison is strategic and does not predict realised voyages or commercial viability.
title: Effects of Route Representation on Distance and Downstream Voyage Implications in Europe–Asia Trade: A Comparison of the Suez, Cape, and Northern Sea Route Corridors

summary: Supporting material for the manuscript "Subacute oral glyphosate impairs testicular function in male mice (Mus musculus): a threshold-anchored dose-response study of steroidogenesis, sperm quality, redox balance and spermatogenic histopathology" (Elbeeh, Filfilan, Filfilan and Filfilan), submitted to Drug and Chemical Toxicology (Taylor & Francis). Forty adult male Swiss albino (ICR) mice, 8-10 weeks old and 22.1-25.5 g at allocation, received vehicle (distilled water) or technical-grade glyphosate at 10, 50 or 100 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for 28 days, n = 10 per group. The dose range brackets the regulatory no-observed-adverse-effect level of approximately 50 mg/kg/day. Endpoints measured in the same 40 animals: body and testis weight; serum testosterone, LH and FSH; epididymal sperm concentration, progressive motility, viability and morphology; testicular malondialdehyde, reduced glutathione, superoxide dismutase and catalase; and testis histopathology stained with haematoxylin-eosin and with periodic acid-Schiff, assessed by the Johnsen tubular-maturation score and by measurement of seminiferous tubule diameter, germinal epithelial height and graded lesion severity. Sections were digitised on a Philips UltraFast Scanner at the x20 level (0.5 micrometres per pixel) and reviewed in the Philips PathologySuite viewer; morphometry was performed in ImageJ v1.54 with semi-automated annotation in QuPath v0.4.3 on fields exported at the native scan resolution. Contents: S1, the manufacturer's Certificate of Analysis for the test article (Sigma-Aldrich 337757, lot MKCZ1523, purity at least 96 per cent, CAS 1071-83-6); S2, analytical kits, instruments, assay conditions and intra- and inter-assay coefficients of variation; S3, the analysis and figure-plotting code; S4, the complete per-animal dataset underlying every figure and table; S5, the benchmark-dose model set with BMD and BMDL10 values; and Supplementary Figure S6 with its caption, showing the histomorphometry and graded lesion scores of Table 4 with individual animal values overlaid. README.md gives the full manifest. Every value reported in the manuscript can be recomputed from S4 using the code in S3. Statistics: continuous endpoints were compared by Welch's ANOVA with the Games-Howell post-hoc test; ordinal lesion grades by the Kruskal-Wallis test with Holm-adjusted Dunn's post-hoc test; monotonic trend by the Jonckheere-Terpstra test; and the endpoint family was controlled at a false-discovery rate of 5 per cent (Benjamini-Hochberg). The Johnsen tubular-maturation score was nominated in advance as the primary endpoint; every other endpoint is secondary. Ethics: all procedures were approved by the Bioethics Committee of Umm Al-Qura University, Makkah, Saudi Arabia (approval no. HAPO-02-K-012-2025-04-2781) and were conducted in accordance with the ARRIVE 2.0 guidelines. These 40 animals also support the cardiotoxicity, neurotoxicity and immunotoxicity arms of the same programme, which are reported separately under the same approval number. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
title: Supplementary data and analysis code for: Subacute oral glyphosate impairs testicular function in male mice (Mus musculus)
